    /\A(?:2\.|3\.0\.[0-2]\z)/.match?(RUBY_VERSION) &&
    caller_locations.any? { |l|
      %r{/(rubygems/gem_runner|bundler/cli)\.rb}.match?(l.path)
    }
  # Before Ruby 3.0.3/3.1.0, the gem and bundle commands used to load
  # the digest library before loading additionally installed gems, so
  # you will get constant redefinition warnings and unexpected
  # implementation overwriting if we proceed here.  Avoid that.
  return
end

require 'digest/version'
require 'digest/loader'

module Digest
  # A mutex for Digest().
  REQUIRE_MUTEX = Thread::Mutex.new

  def self.const_missing(name) # :nodoc:
    case name
    when :SHA256, :SHA384, :SHA512
      lib = 'digest/sha2'
    else
      lib = File.join('digest', name.to_s.downcase)
    end

    begin
      require lib
    rescue LoadError
      raise LoadError, "library not found for class Digest::#{name} -- #{lib}", caller(1)
    end
    unless Digest.const_defined?(name)
      raise NameError, "uninitialized constant Digest::#{name}", caller(1)
    end
    Digest.const_get(name)
  end

  class ::Digest::Class
    # Creates a digest object and reads a given file, _name_.
    # Optional arguments are passed to the constructor of the digest
    # class.
    #
    #   p Digest::SHA256.file("X11R6.8.2-src.tar.bz2").hexdigest
    #   # => "f02e3c85572dc9ad7cb77c2a638e3be24cc1b5bea9fdbb0b0299c9668475c534"
    def self.file(name, *args)
      new(*args).file(name)
    end

    # Returns the base64 encoded hash value of a given _string_.  The
    # return value is properly padded with '=' and contains no line
    # feeds.
    def self.base64digest(str, *args)
      [digest(str, *args)].pack('m0')
    end
  end

  module Instance
    # Updates the digest with the contents of a given file _name_ and
    # returns self.
    def file(name)
      File.open(name, "rb") {|f|
        buf = ""
        while f.read(16384, buf)
          update buf
        end
      }
      self
    end

    # If none is given, returns the resulting hash value of the digest
    # in a base64 encoded form, keeping the digest's state.
    #
    # If a +string+ is given, returns the hash value for the given
    # +string+ in a base64 encoded form, resetting the digest to the
    # initial state before and after the process.
    #
    # In either case, the return value is properly padded with '=' and
    # contains no line feeds.
    def base64digest(str = nil)
      [str ? digest(str) : digest].pack('m0')
    end

    # Returns the resulting hash value and resets the digest to the
    # initial state.
    def base64digest!
      [digest!].pack('m0')
    end
  end
end

# call-seq:
#   Digest(name) -> digest_subclass
#
# Returns a Digest subclass by +name+ in a thread-safe manner even
# when on-demand loading is involved.
#
#   require 'digest'
#
#   Digest("MD5")
#   # => Digest::MD5
#
#   Digest(:SHA256)
#   # => Digest::SHA256
#
#   Digest(:Foo)
#   # => LoadError: library not found for class Digest::Foo -- digest/foo
def Digest(name)
  const = name.to_sym
  Digest::REQUIRE_MUTEX.synchronize {
    # Ignore autoload's because it is void when we have #const_missing
    Digest.const_missing(const)
  }
rescue LoadError
  # Constants do not necessarily rely on digest/*.
  if Digest.const_defined?(const)
    Digest.const_get(const)
  else
    raise
  end
end

require 'json/common'

##
# = JavaScript \Object Notation (\JSON)
#
# \JSON is a lightweight data-interchange format.
#
# A \JSON value is one of the following:
# - Double-quoted text:  <tt>"foo"</tt>.
# - Number:  +1+, +1.0+, +2.0e2+.
# - Boolean:  +true+, +false+.
# - Null: +null+.
# - \Array: an ordered list of values, enclosed by square brackets:
#     ["foo", 1, 1.0, 2.0e2, true, false, null]
#
# - \Object: a collection of name/value pairs, enclosed by curly braces;
#   each name is double-quoted text;
#   the values may be any \JSON values:
#     {"a": "foo", "b": 1, "c": 1.0, "d": 2.0e2, "e": true, "f": false, "g": null}
#
# A \JSON array or object may contain nested arrays, objects, and scalars
# to any depth:
#   {"foo": {"bar": 1, "baz": 2}, "bat": [0, 1, 2]}
#   [{"foo": 0, "bar": 1}, ["baz", 2]]
#
# == Using \Module \JSON
#
# To make module \JSON available in your code, begin with:
#   require 'json'
#
# All examples here assume that this has been done.
#
# === Parsing \JSON
#
# You can parse a \String containing \JSON data using
# either of two methods:
# - <tt>JSON.parse(source, opts)</tt>
# - <tt>JSON.parse!(source, opts)</tt>
#
# where
# - +source+ is a Ruby object.
# - +opts+ is a \Hash object containing options
#   that control both input allowed and output formatting.
#
# The difference between the two methods
# is that JSON.parse! omits some checks
# and may not be safe for some +source+ data;
# use it only for data from trusted sources.
# Use the safer method JSON.parse for less trusted sources.
#
# ==== Parsing \JSON Arrays
#
# When +source+ is a \JSON array, JSON.parse by default returns a Ruby \Array:
#   json = '["foo", 1, 1.0, 2.0e2, true, false, null]'
#   ruby = JSON.parse(json)
#   ruby # => ["foo", 1, 1.0, 200.0, true, false, nil]
#   ruby.class # => Array
#
# The \JSON array may contain nested arrays, objects, and scalars
# to any depth:
#   json = '[{"foo": 0, "bar": 1}, ["baz", 2]]'
#   JSON.parse(json) # => [{"foo"=>0, "bar"=>1}, ["baz", 2]]
#
# ==== Parsing \JSON \Objects
#
# When the source is a \JSON object, JSON.parse by default returns a Ruby \Hash:
#   json = '{"a": "foo", "b": 1, "c": 1.0, "d": 2.0e2, "e": true, "f": false, "g": null}'
#   ruby = JSON.parse(json)
#   ruby # => {"a"=>"foo", "b"=>1, "c"=>1.0, "d"=>200.0, "e"=>true, "f"=>false, "g"=>nil}
#   ruby.class # => Hash
#
# The \JSON object may contain nested arrays, objects, and scalars
# to any depth:
#   json = '{"foo": {"bar": 1, "baz": 2}, "bat": [0, 1, 2]}'
#   JSON.parse(json) # => {"foo"=>{"bar"=>1, "baz"=>2}, "bat"=>[0, 1, 2]}
#
# ==== Parsing \JSON Scalars
#
# When the source is a \JSON scalar (not an array or object),
# JSON.parse returns a Ruby scalar.
#
# \String:
#   ruby = JSON.parse('"foo"')
#   ruby # => 'foo'
#   ruby.class # => String
# \Integer:
#   ruby = JSON.parse('1')
#   ruby # => 1
#   ruby.class # => Integer
# \Float:
#   ruby = JSON.parse('1.0')
#   ruby # => 1.0
#   ruby.class # => Float
#   ruby = JSON.parse('2.0e2')
#   ruby # => 200
#   ruby.class # => Float
# Boolean:
#   ruby = JSON.parse('true')
#   ruby # => true
#   ruby.class # => TrueClass
#   ruby = JSON.parse('false')
#   ruby # => false
#   ruby.class # => FalseClass
# Null:
#   ruby = JSON.parse('null')
#   ruby # => nil
#   ruby.class # => NilClass
#
# ==== Parsing Options
#
# ====== Input Options
#
# Option +max_nesting+ (\Integer) specifies the maximum nesting depth allowed;
# defaults to +100+; specify +false+ to disable depth checking.
#
# With the default, +false+:
#   source = '[0, [1, [2, [3]]]]'
#   ruby = JSON.parse(source)
#   ruby # => [0, [1, [2, [3]]]]
# Too deep:
#   # Raises JSON::NestingError (nesting of 2 is too deep):
#   JSON.parse(source, {max_nesting: 1})
# Bad value:
#   # Raises TypeError (wrong argument type Symbol (expected Fixnum)):
#   JSON.parse(source, {max_nesting: :foo})
#
# ---
#
# Option +allow_nan+ (boolean) specifies whether to allow
# NaN, Infinity, and MinusInfinity in +source+;
# defaults to +false+.
#
# With the default, +false+:
#   # Raises JSON::ParserError (225: unexpected token at '[NaN]'):
#   JSON.parse('[NaN]')
#   # Raises JSON::ParserError (232: unexpected token at '[Infinity]'):
#   JSON.parse('[Infinity]')
#   # Raises JSON::ParserError (248: unexpected token at '[-Infinity]'):
#   JSON.parse('[-Infinity]')
# Allow:
#   source = '[NaN, Infinity, -Infinity]'
#   ruby = JSON.parse(source, {allow_nan: true})
#   ruby # => [NaN, Infinity, -Infinity]
#
# ====== Output Options
#
# Option +symbolize_names+ (boolean) specifies whether returned \Hash keys
# should be Symbols;
# defaults to +false+ (use Strings).
#
# With the default, +false+:
#   source = '{"a": "foo", "b": 1.0, "c": true, "d": false, "e": null}'
#   ruby = JSON.parse(source)
#   ruby # => {"a"=>"foo", "b"=>1.0, "c"=>true, "d"=>false, "e"=>nil}
# Use Symbols:
#   ruby = JSON.parse(source, {symbolize_names: true})
#   ruby # => {:a=>"foo", :b=>1.0, :c=>true, :d=>false, :e=>nil}
#
# ---
#
# Option +object_class+ (\Class) specifies the Ruby class to be used
# for each \JSON object;
# defaults to \Hash.
#
# With the default, \Hash:
#   source = '{"a": "foo", "b": 1.0, "c": true, "d": false, "e": null}'
#   ruby = JSON.parse(source)
#   ruby.class # => Hash
# Use class \OpenStruct:
#   ruby = JSON.parse(source, {object_class: OpenStruct})
#   ruby # => #<OpenStruct a="foo", b=1.0, c=true, d=false, e=nil>
#
# ---
#
# Option +array_class+ (\Class) specifies the Ruby class to be used
# for each \JSON array;
# defaults to \Array.
#
# With the default, \Array:
#   source = '["foo", 1.0, true, false, null]'
#   ruby = JSON.parse(source)
#   ruby.class # => Array
# Use class \Set:
#   ruby = JSON.parse(source, {array_class: Set})
#   ruby # => #<Set: {"foo", 1.0, true, false, nil}>
#
# ---
#
# Option +create_additions+ (boolean) specifies whether to use \JSON additions in parsing.
# See {\JSON Additions}[#module-JSON-label-JSON+Additions].
#
# === Generating \JSON
#
# To generate a Ruby \String containing \JSON data,
# use method <tt>JSON.generate(source, opts)</tt>, where
# - +source+ is a Ruby object.
# - +opts+ is a \Hash object containing options
#   that control both input allowed and output formatting.
#
# ==== Generating \JSON from Arrays
#
# When the source is a Ruby \Array, JSON.generate returns
# a \String containing a \JSON array:
#   ruby = [0, 's', :foo]
#   json = JSON.generate(ruby)
#   json # => '[0,"s","foo"]'
#
# The Ruby \Array array may contain nested arrays, hashes, and scalars
# to any depth:
#   ruby = [0, [1, 2], {foo: 3, bar: 4}]
#   json = JSON.generate(ruby)
#   json # => '[0,[1,2],{"foo":3,"bar":4}]'
#
# ==== Generating \JSON from Hashes
#
# When the source is a Ruby \Hash, JSON.generate returns
# a \String containing a \JSON object:
#   ruby = {foo: 0, bar: 's', baz: :bat}
#   json = JSON.generate(ruby)
#   json # => '{"foo":0,"bar":"s","baz":"bat"}'
#
# The Ruby \Hash array may contain nested arrays, hashes, and scalars
# to any depth:
#   ruby = {foo: [0, 1], bar: {baz: 2, bat: 3}, bam: :bad}
#   json = JSON.generate(ruby)
#   json # => '{"foo":[0,1],"bar":{"baz":2,"bat":3},"bam":"bad"}'
#
# ==== Generating \JSON from Other Objects
#
# When the source is neither an \Array nor a \Hash,
# the generated \JSON data depends on the class of the source.
#
# When the source is a Ruby \Integer or \Float, JSON.generate returns
# a \String containing a \JSON number:
#   JSON.generate(42) # => '42'
#   JSON.generate(0.42) # => '0.42'
#
# When the source is a Ruby \String, JSON.generate returns
# a \String containing a \JSON string (with double-quotes):
#   JSON.generate('A string') # => '"A string"'
#
# When the source is +true+, +false+ or +nil+, JSON.generate returns
# a \String containing the corresponding \JSON token:
#   JSON.generate(true) # => 'true'
#   JSON.generate(false) # => 'false'
#   JSON.generate(nil) # => 'null'
#
# When the source is none of the above, JSON.generate returns
# a \String containing a \JSON string representation of the source:
#   JSON.generate(:foo) # => '"foo"'
#   JSON.generate(Complex(0, 0)) # => '"0+0i"'
#   JSON.generate(Dir.new('.')) # => '"#<Dir>"'
#
# ==== Generating Options
#
# ====== Input Options
#
# Option +allow_nan+ (boolean) specifies whether
# +NaN+, +Infinity+, and <tt>-Infinity</tt> may be generated;
# defaults to +false+.
#
# With the default, +false+:
#   # Raises JSON::GeneratorError (920: NaN not allowed in JSON):
#   JSON.generate(JSON::NaN)
#   # Raises JSON::GeneratorError (917: Infinity not allowed in JSON):
#   JSON.generate(JSON::Infinity)
#   # Raises JSON::GeneratorError (917: -Infinity not allowed in JSON):
#   JSON.generate(JSON::MinusInfinity)
#
# Allow:
#   ruby = [Float::NaN, Float::Infinity, Float::MinusInfinity]
#   JSON.generate(ruby, allow_nan: true) # => '[NaN,Infinity,-Infinity]'
#
# ---
#
# Option +max_nesting+ (\Integer) specifies the maximum nesting depth
# in +obj+; defaults to +100+.
#
# With the default, +100+:
#   obj = [[[[[[0]]]]]]
#   JSON.generate(obj) # => '[[[[[[0]]]]]]'
#
# Too deep:
#   # Raises JSON::NestingError (nesting of 2 is too deep):
#   JSON.generate(obj, max_nesting: 2)
#
# ====== Escaping Options
#
# Options +script_safe+ (boolean) specifies wether <tt>'\u2028'</tt>, <tt>'\u2029'</tt>
# and <tt>'/'</tt> should be escaped as to make the JSON object safe to interpolate in script
# tags.
#
# Options +ascii_only+ (boolean) specifies wether all characters outside the ASCII range
# should be escaped.
#
# ====== Output Options
#
# The default formatting options generate the most compact
# \JSON data, all on one line and with no whitespace.
#
# You can use these formatting options to generate
# \JSON data in a more open format, using whitespace.
# See also JSON.pretty_generate.
#
# - Option +array_nl+ (\String) specifies a string (usually a newline)
#   to be inserted after each \JSON array; defaults to the empty \String, <tt>''</tt>.
# - Option +object_nl+ (\String) specifies a string (usually a newline)
#   to be inserted after each \JSON object; defaults to the empty \String, <tt>''</tt>.
# - Option +indent+ (\String) specifies the string (usually spaces) to be
#   used for indentation; defaults to the empty \String, <tt>''</tt>;
#   defaults to the empty \String, <tt>''</tt>;
#   has no effect unless options +array_nl+ or +object_nl+ specify newlines.
# - Option +space+ (\String) specifies a string (usually a space) to be
#   inserted after the colon in each \JSON object's pair;
#   defaults to the empty \String, <tt>''</tt>.
# - Option +space_before+ (\String) specifies a string (usually a space) to be
#   inserted before the colon in each \JSON object's pair;
#   defaults to the empty \String, <tt>''</tt>.
#
# In this example, +obj+ is used first to generate the shortest
# \JSON data (no whitespace), then again with all formatting options
# specified:
#
#   obj = {foo: [:bar, :baz], bat: {bam: 0, bad: 1}}
#   json = JSON.generate(obj)
#   puts 'Compact:', json
#   opts = {
#     array_nl: "\n",
#     object_nl: "\n",
#     indent: '  ',
#     space_before: ' ',
#     space: ' '
#   }
#   puts 'Open:', JSON.generate(obj, opts)
#
# Output:
#   Compact:
#   {"foo":["bar","baz"],"bat":{"bam":0,"bad":1}}
#   Open:
#   {
#     "foo" : [
#       "bar",
#       "baz"
#   ],
#     "bat" : {
#       "bam" : 0,
#       "bad" : 1
#     }
#   }
#
# == \JSON Additions
#
# When you "round trip" a non-\String object from Ruby to \JSON and back,
# you have a new \String, instead of the object you began with:
#   ruby0 = Range.new(0, 2)
#   json = JSON.generate(ruby0)
#   json # => '0..2"'
#   ruby1 = JSON.parse(json)
#   ruby1 # => '0..2'
#   ruby1.class # => String
#
# You can use \JSON _additions_ to preserve the original object.
# The addition is an extension of a ruby class, so that:
# - \JSON.generate stores more information in the \JSON string.
# - \JSON.parse, called with option +create_additions+,
#   uses that information to create a proper Ruby object.
#
# This example shows a \Range being generated into \JSON
# and parsed back into Ruby, both without and with
# the addition for \Range:
#   ruby = Range.new(0, 2)
#   # This passage does not use the addition for Range.
#   json0 = JSON.generate(ruby)
#   ruby0 = JSON.parse(json0)
#   # This passage uses the addition for Range.
#   require 'json/add/range'
#   json1 = JSON.generate(ruby)
#   ruby1 = JSON.parse(json1, create_additions: true)
#   # Make a nice display.
#   display = <<~EOT
#     Generated JSON:
#       Without addition:  #{json0} (#{json0.class})
#       With addition:     #{json1} (#{json1.class})
#     Parsed JSON:
#       Without addition:  #{ruby0.inspect} (#{ruby0.class})
#       With addition:     #{ruby1.inspect} (#{ruby1.class})
#   EOT
#   puts display
#
# This output shows the different results:
#   Generated JSON:
#     Without addition:  "0..2" (String)
#     With addition:     {"json_class":"Range","a":[0,2,false]} (String)
#   Parsed JSON:
#     Without addition:  "0..2" (String)
#     With addition:     0..2 (Range)
#
# The \JSON module includes additions for certain classes.
# You can also craft custom additions.
# See {Custom \JSON Additions}[#module-JSON-label-Custom+JSON+Additions].
#
# === Built-in Additions
#
# The \JSON module includes additions for certain classes.
# To use an addition, +require+ its source:
# - BigDecimal: <tt>require 'json/add/bigdecimal'</tt>
# - Complex: <tt>require 'json/add/complex'</tt>
# - Date: <tt>require 'json/add/date'</tt>
# - DateTime: <tt>require 'json/add/date_time'</tt>
# - Exception: <tt>require 'json/add/exception'</tt>
# - OpenStruct: <tt>require 'json/add/ostruct'</tt>
# - Range: <tt>require 'json/add/range'</tt>
# - Rational: <tt>require 'json/add/rational'</tt>
# - Regexp: <tt>require 'json/add/regexp'</tt>
# - Set: <tt>require 'json/add/set'</tt>
# - Struct: <tt>require 'json/add/struct'</tt>
# - Symbol: <tt>require 'json/add/symbol'</tt>
# - Time: <tt>require 'json/add/time'</tt>
#
# To reduce punctuation clutter, the examples below
# show the generated \JSON via +puts+, rather than the usual +inspect+,
#
# \BigDecimal:
#   require 'json/add/bigdecimal'
#   ruby0 = BigDecimal(0) # 0.0
#   json = JSON.generate(ruby0) # {"json_class":"BigDecimal","b":"27:0.0"}
#   ruby1 = JSON.parse(json, create_additions: true) # 0.0
#   ruby1.class # => BigDecimal
#
# \Complex:
#   require 'json/add/complex'
#   ruby0 = Complex(1+0i) # 1+0i
#   json = JSON.generate(ruby0) # {"json_class":"Complex","r":1,"i":0}
#   ruby1 = JSON.parse(json, create_additions: true) # 1+0i
#   ruby1.class # Complex
#
# \Date:
#   require 'json/add/date'
#   ruby0 = Date.today # 2020-05-02
#   json = JSON.generate(ruby0) # {"json_class":"Date","y":2020,"m":5,"d":2,"sg":2299161.0}
#   ruby1 = JSON.parse(json, create_additions: true) # 2020-05-02
#   ruby1.class # Date
#
# \DateTime:
#   require 'json/add/date_time'
#   ruby0 = DateTime.now # 2020-05-02T10:38:13-05:00
#   json = JSON.generate(ruby0) # {"json_class":"DateTime","y":2020,"m":5,"d":2,"H":10,"M":38,"S":13,"of":"-5/24","sg":2299161.0}
#   ruby1 = JSON.parse(json, create_additions: true) # 2020-05-02T10:38:13-05:00
#   ruby1.class # DateTime
#
# \Exception (and its subclasses including \RuntimeError):
#   require 'json/add/exception'
#   ruby0 = Exception.new('A message') # A message
#   json = JSON.generate(ruby0) # {"json_class":"Exception","m":"A message","b":null}
#   ruby1 = JSON.parse(json, create_additions: true) # A message
#   ruby1.class # Exception
#   ruby0 = RuntimeError.new('Another message') # Another message
#   json = JSON.generate(ruby0) # {"json_class":"RuntimeError","m":"Another message","b":null}
#   ruby1 = JSON.parse(json, create_additions: true) # Another message
#   ruby1.class # RuntimeError
#
# \OpenStruct:
#   require 'json/add/ostruct'
#   ruby0 = OpenStruct.new(name: 'Matz', language: 'Ruby') # #<OpenStruct name="Matz", language="Ruby">
#   json = JSON.generate(ruby0) # {"json_class":"OpenStruct","t":{"name":"Matz","language":"Ruby"}}
#   ruby1 = JSON.parse(json, create_additions: true) # #<OpenStruct name="Matz", language="Ruby">
#   ruby1.class # OpenStruct
#
# \Range:
#   require 'json/add/range'
#   ruby0 = Range.new(0, 2) # 0..2
#   json = JSON.generate(ruby0) # {"json_class":"Range","a":[0,2,false]}
#   ruby1 = JSON.parse(json, create_additions: true) # 0..2
#   ruby1.class # Range
#
# \Rational:
#   require 'json/add/rational'
#   ruby0 = Rational(1, 3) # 1/3
#   json = JSON.generate(ruby0) # {"json_class":"Rational","n":1,"d":3}
#   ruby1 = JSON.parse(json, create_additions: true) # 1/3
#   ruby1.class # Rational
#
# \Regexp:
#   require 'json/add/regexp'
#   ruby0 = Regexp.new('foo') # (?-mix:foo)
#   json = JSON.generate(ruby0) # {"json_class":"Regexp","o":0,"s":"foo"}
#   ruby1 = JSON.parse(json, create_additions: true) # (?-mix:foo)
#   ruby1.class # Regexp
#
# \Set:
#   require 'json/add/set'
#   ruby0 = Set.new([0, 1, 2]) # #<Set: {0, 1, 2}>
#   json = JSON.generate(ruby0) # {"json_class":"Set","a":[0,1,2]}
#   ruby1 = JSON.parse(json, create_additions: true) # #<Set: {0, 1, 2}>
#   ruby1.class # Set
#
# \Struct:
#   require 'json/add/struct'
#   Customer = Struct.new(:name, :address) # Customer
#   ruby0 = Customer.new("Dave", "123 Main") # #<struct Customer name="Dave", address="123 Main">
#   json = JSON.generate(ruby0) # {"json_class":"Customer","v":["Dave","123 Main"]}
#   ruby1 = JSON.parse(json, create_additions: true) # #<struct Customer name="Dave", address="123 Main">
#   ruby1.class # Customer
#
# \Symbol:
#   require 'json/add/symbol'
#   ruby0 = :foo # foo
#   json = JSON.generate(ruby0) # {"json_class":"Symbol","s":"foo"}
#   ruby1 = JSON.parse(json, create_additions: true) # foo
#   ruby1.class # Symbol
#

  # - Recursively calls <tt>proc(result)</tt>.

  def load(source, proc = nil, options = nil)

      load_default_options
    else
      load_default_options.merge(options)
    end

    unless source.is_a?(String)
      if source.respond_to? :to_str
        source = source.to_str
      elsif source.respond_to? :to_io
        source = source.to_io.read
      elsif source.respond_to?(:read)
        source = source.read
      end
    end

    if opts[:allow_blank] && (source.nil? || source.empty?)
      source = 'null'
    end
    result = parse(source, opts)
    recurse_proc(result, &proc) if proc
    result

  def recurse_proc(result, &proc) # :nodoc:
    case result
    when Array
      result.each { |x| recurse_proc x, &proc }
      proc.call result
    when Hash
      result.each { |x, y| recurse_proc x, &proc; recurse_proc y, &proc }
      proc.call result
    else
      proc.call result
    end

    # Initially:
    #   opts = JSON.dump_default_options

    :max_nesting => false,
    :allow_nan   => true,
  }

  # :call-seq:
  #   JSON.dump(obj, io = nil, limit = nil)
  #
  # Dumps +obj+ as a \JSON string, i.e. calls generate on the object and returns the result.
  #
  # The default options can be changed via method JSON.dump_default_options.
  #
  # - Argument +io+, if given, should respond to method +write+;
  #   the \JSON \String is written to +io+, and +io+ is returned.
  #   If +io+ is not given, the \JSON \String is returned.
  # - Argument +limit+, if given, is passed to JSON.generate as option +max_nesting+.
  #
  # ---
  #
  # When argument +io+ is not given, returns the \JSON \String generated from +obj+:
  #   obj = {foo: [0, 1], bar: {baz: 2, bat: 3}, bam: :bad}
  #   json = JSON.dump(obj)
  #   json # => "{\"foo\":[0,1],\"bar\":{\"baz\":2,\"bat\":3},\"bam\":\"bad\"}"
  #
  # When argument +io+ is given, writes the \JSON \String to +io+ and returns +io+:
  #   path = 't.json'
  #   File.open(path, 'w') do |file|
  #     JSON.dump(obj, file)
  #   end # => #<File:t.json (closed)>
  #   puts File.read(path)
  # Output:
  #   {"foo":[0,1],"bar":{"baz":2,"bat":3},"bam":"bad"}
  def dump(obj, anIO = nil, limit = nil, kwargs = nil)
    if kwargs.nil?
      if limit.nil?
        if anIO.is_a?(Hash)
          kwargs = anIO
          anIO = nil
        end
      elsif limit.is_a?(Hash)
        kwargs = limit
        limit = nil
      end
    end

    unless anIO.nil?
      if anIO.respond_to?(:to_io)
        anIO = anIO.to_io
      elsif limit.nil? && !anIO.respond_to?(:write)
        anIO, limit = nil, anIO
      end
    end

    opts = JSON.dump_default_options
    opts = opts.merge(:max_nesting => limit) if limit
    opts = merge_dump_options(opts, **kwargs) if kwargs

    begin
      if State === opts
        opts.generate(obj, anIO)
      else
        State.generate(obj, opts, anIO)
      end
    rescue JSON::NestingError
      raise ArgumentError, "exceed depth limit"
    end
  end

  # Encodes string using String.encode.
  def self.iconv(to, from, string)
    string.encode(to, from)
  end

  def merge_dump_options(opts, strict: NOT_SET)
    opts = opts.merge(strict: strict) if NOT_SET != strict
    opts
  end

  class << self
    private :merge_dump_options
  end
end

module ::Kernel
  private

  # Outputs _objs_ to STDOUT as JSON strings in the shortest form, that is in
  # one line.
  def j(*objs)
    objs.each do |obj|
      puts JSON::generate(obj, :allow_nan => true, :max_nesting => false)
    end
    nil
  end

  # Outputs _objs_ to STDOUT as JSON strings in a pretty format, with
  # indentation and over many lines.
  def jj(*objs)
    objs.each do |obj|
      puts JSON::pretty_generate(obj, :allow_nan => true, :max_nesting => false)
    end
    nil
  end

  # If _object_ is string-like, parse the string and return the parsed result as
  # a Ruby data structure. Otherwise, generate a JSON text from the Ruby data
  # structure object and return it.
  #
  # The _opts_ argument is passed through to generate/parse respectively. See
  # generate and parse for their documentation.
  def JSON(object, *args)
    if object.is_a?(String)
      return JSON.parse(object, args.first)
    elsif object.respond_to?(:to_str)
      str = object.to_str
      if str.is_a?(String)
        return JSON.parse(object.to_str, args.first)
      end
    end

    JSON.generate(object, args.first)
  end
end

class ::Class
  # Returns true if this class can be used to create an instance

  # method _json_create_ that expects a hash as first parameter. The hash
  # should include the required data.
  def json_creatable?
    respond_to?(:json_create)
  end
end

      class State
        # call-seq: new(opts = {})
        #
        # Instantiates a new State object, configured by _opts_.
        #
        # _opts_ can have the following keys:
        #
        # * *indent*: a string used to indent levels (default: ''),
        # * *space*: a string that is put after, a : or , delimiter (default: ''),
        # * *space_before*: a string that is put before a : pair delimiter (default: ''),
        # * *object_nl*: a string that is put at the end of a JSON object (default: ''),
        # * *array_nl*: a string that is put at the end of a JSON array (default: ''),
        # * *allow_nan*: true if NaN, Infinity, and -Infinity should be
        #   generated, otherwise an exception is thrown, if these values are
        #   encountered. This options defaults to false.
        # * *ascii_only*: true if only ASCII characters should be generated. This
        #   option defaults to false.
        # * *buffer_initial_length*: sets the initial length of the generator's
        #   internal buffer.
        def initialize(opts = nil)
          if opts && !opts.empty?
            configure(opts)
          end
        end

        # call-seq: configure(opts)
        #
        # Configure this State instance with the Hash _opts_, and return
        # itself.
        def configure(opts)
          unless opts.is_a?(Hash)
            if opts.respond_to?(:to_hash)
              opts = opts.to_hash
            elsif opts.respond_to?(:to_h)
              opts = opts.to_h
            else
              raise TypeError, "can't convert #{opts.class} into Hash"
            end
          end
          _configure(opts)
        end

        alias_method :merge, :configure

        # call-seq:
        #   generate(obj) -> String
        #   generate(obj, anIO) -> anIO
        #
        # Generates a valid JSON document from object +obj+ and returns the
        # result. If no valid JSON document can be created this method raises a
        # GeneratorError exception.
        def generate(obj, io = nil)
          _generate(obj, io)
        end

        # call-seq: to_h
        #
        # Returns the configuration instance variables as a hash, that can be
        # passed to the configure method.
        def to_h
          result = {
            indent: indent,
            space: space,
            space_before: space_before,
            object_nl: object_nl,
            array_nl: array_nl,
            allow_nan: allow_nan?,
            ascii_only: ascii_only?,
            max_nesting: max_nesting,
            script_safe: script_safe?,
            strict: strict?,
            depth: depth,
            buffer_initial_length: buffer_initial_length,
          }

          instance_variables.each do |iv|
            iv = iv.to_s[1..-1]
            result[iv.to_sym] = self[iv]
          end

          result
        end

        alias_method :to_hash, :to_h

        # call-seq: [](name)
        #
        # Returns the value returned by method +name+.
        def [](name)
          if respond_to?(name)
            __send__(name)
          else
            instance_variable_get("@#{name}") if
              instance_variables.include?("@#{name}".to_sym) # avoid warning
          end
        end

        # call-seq: []=(name, value)
        #
        # Sets the attribute name to value.
        def []=(name, value)
          if respond_to?(name_writer = "#{name}=")
            __send__ name_writer, value
          else
            instance_variable_set "@#{name}", value
          end
        end
      end
    end
  end

        when object.respond_to?(:to_hash)
          result = new
          object.to_hash.each do |key, value|
            result[key] = from_hash(value)
          end
          result
        when object.respond_to?(:to_ary)
          object.to_ary.map { |a| from_hash(a) }
        else
          object
        end
      end

        result = ::JSON.load(source, proc, opts.merge(:object_class => self))

      end

      end

      def self.preset(key)
        pr = PRESETS[key] or return normalize({})
        p = deep_copy(pr)
        # Kitchen modules: back set in between the sides, flush with their rear edge.
        p = KITCHEN.merge(p) if pr['label'].to_s.start_with?('Kitchen')
        p.delete('label')
        p['type'] = key
        p['top_outside'] = true
        # Loose panel: its thickness is one of the three sizes, so W × H × D is always the panel's outside.
        if p['panel']
          case p['panel_kind']
          when 'top', 'bottom' then p['height'] = p['panel_t']
          when 'side' then p['width'] = p['panel_t']
          else p['depth'] = p['panel_t']
          end
        end
        normalize(p)
      end

      def self.num(v, fallback)
        return v.to_f if v.is_a?(Numeric)
        s = v.to_s.strip.tr(',', '.')
        s =~ /\A-?\d+(\.\d+)?\z/ ? s.to_f : fallback.to_f
      end

      # 'auto' (or blank) stays 'auto', anything numeric becomes a Float.
      def self.size_spec(v)
        return v.to_f if v.is_a?(Numeric)
        s = v.to_s.strip.tr(',', '.')
        s =~ /\A\d+(\.\d+)?\z/ && s.to_f > 0 ? s.to_f : 'auto'
      end

      def self.normalize(input)
        input = {} unless input.is_a?(Hash)
        p = deep_copy(DEFAULTS)
        input.each { |k, v| p[k.to_s] = deep_copy(v) }

        # Modules saved before the back options existed only have back_type / back_t.
        if !input.key?('back_mount') && input.key?('back_type')
          old = input['back_type'].to_s
          p['back_mount'] = old == 'applied' ? 'applied' : 'inset'
          p['back_slot'] = old == 'groove'
          p['back_t_same'] = false unless input.key?('back_t_same')
        elsif !input.key?('back_t_same') && input.key?('back_t')
          p['back_t_same'] = num(input['back_t'], 0) == num(input['t'] || DEFAULTS['t'], 0)
        end
        # Saved before 0.2.1 (no "same" flags): a value equal to the carcass one stays linked,
        # anything else keeps its own value.
        SAME_T.each do |k|
          next if input.key?("#{k}_same") || !input.key?(k)
          p["#{k}_same"] = num(input[k], 0) == num(input['t'] || DEFAULTS['t'], 0)
        end
        SAME_MAT.each do |k|
          next if input.key?("#{k}_same") || !input.key?(k)
          old = OLD_MATERIALS[input[k].to_s] || input[k].to_s
          car = OLD_MATERIALS[input['mat_carcass'].to_s] || (input['mat_carcass'] || DEFAULTS['mat_carcass']).to_s
          p["#{k}_same"] = old == car
        end

        # Saved before 0.3.13 (box systems had only typed sizes): keep them as typed.
        p['bx_custom'] = true if !input.key?('bx_custom') && input.key?('bx_side_h')
        # Saved before 0.3.17 (drawers always opened all the way): keep that.
        p['drawer_open'] = 'full' if !input.key?('drawer_open') && input.key?('drawer_ext')
        # Saved before 0.3.13 (bottoms were always slotted): keep them slotted.
        p['db_bottom_fit'] = 'slotted' if !input.key?('db_bottom_fit') && input.key?('db_bottom_t')
        # Saved before 0.3.11 (no plastic kick option): keep the board toe kick.
        p['kick_plastic'] = false if !input.key?('kick_plastic') && input.key?('mat_kick')
        # Before 0.1.6 one orientation/width served both stretchers.
        if input.key?('stretcher_orient') && !input.key?('front_stretcher_orient')
          p['front_stretcher_orient'] = p['stretcher_orient']
          p['rear_stretcher_orient'] = p['stretcher_orient'] unless input.key?('rear_stretcher_orient')
        end
        p['rear_stretcher_w'] = p['stretcher_w'] unless input.key?('rear_stretcher_w')
        MAT_KEYS.each { |k| p[k] = OLD_MATERIALS[p[k].to_s] || p[k] }

        NUMERIC_KEYS.each { |k| p[k] = num(p[k], DEFAULTS[k]) }
        p['door_angle'] = p['door_angle'].clamp(10.0, 180.0)
        p['lift_angle'] = p['lift_angle'].clamp(10.0, 120.0)
        p['flap_angle'] = p['flap_angle'].clamp(10.0, 100.0)
        p['drawer_ext'] = p['drawer_ext'].clamp(10.0, 100.0)
        (BOOL_KEYS + SAME_T.map { |k| "#{k}_same" } + SAME_MAT.map { |k| "#{k}_same" }).each { |k| p[k] = (p[k] == true || p[k].to_s == 'true') }
        CHOICES.each { |k, opts| p[k] = DEFAULTS[k] unless opts.include?(p[k].to_s) }
        p['back_t'] = p['t'] if p['back_t_same']
        unless p['bx_custom']
          bs = box_system(p)
          p['bx_height'] = 'M' unless bs['heights'].key?(p['bx_height'])
          side = bs['heights'][p['bx_height']]
          p['bx_side_h'] = side
          p['bx_bottom_w_deduct'] = bs['bottom_w']
          p['bx_bottom_d_deduct'] = bs['bottom_d']
          p['bx_back_w_deduct'] = bs['back_w']
          p['bx_back_h'] = p['bx_gallery'] ? p['bx_gallery_back'].to_f : side - bs['back_off']
        end
        SAME_T.each { |k| p[k] = p['t'] if p["#{k}_same"] }
        p['skin_t'] = p['t'] if p['skin_t_same']
        SAME_MAT.each { |k| p[k] = p['mat_carcass'] if p["#{k}_same"] }
        p['mat_end'] = p['mat_front'] if p['mat_end_same']
        # Applied back options and visible top / bottom / back: stored only when used (codes unchanged)
        %w[back_floor back_hset back_over end_top end_bottom end_back].each do |k|
          if p[k] == true || p[k] == 'true' then p[k] = true else p.delete(k) end
        end
        if p['back_hset']
          p['back_h'] = num(p['back_h'], 0)
          p['back_h'] = p['height'].to_f if p['back_h'] <= 0
        else
          p.delete('back_h')
          p.delete('back_over')
        end
        # Lower boxes' top at a split: stretchers unless full panel is chosen (stored only then)
        if p['split_top'].to_s == 'full_panel' then p['split_top'] = 'full_panel' else p.delete('split_top') end
        # Clothes hangers on the rails (look only): stored only when not the usual amount
        if %w[off half full].include?(p['hangers'].to_s) then p['hangers'] = p['hangers'].to_s else p.delete('hangers') end
        # Decorative back: stored only when ticked (older modules keep their codes)
        if p['skin_b'] == true || p['skin_b'] == 'true' then p['skin_b'] = true else p.delete('skin_b') end
        # Back "same as fronts" (stored only when ticked, so older modules keep their codes)
        if p['mat_back_front'] == true || p['mat_back_front'] == 'true'
          p['mat_back_front'] = true
          p['mat_back_same'] = false
          p['mat_back'] = p['mat_front']
        else
          p.delete('mat_back_front')
        end
        { 'back_recess' => 'back_recess_mode', 'kick_setback' => 'kick_setback_mode' }.each do |k, mk|
          n = { '1T' => 1, '2T' => 2 }[p[mk]]
          p[k] = p['t'] * n if n
        end
        # Before 0.2.2 the solid top sat inside the module height. It is now a decorative
        # top on the carcass, outside the height: keep old modules the same overall size.
        if !input.key?('top_outside') && input.key?('height') && p['add_top']
          p['height'] = p['height'] - p['top_t']
        end
        p['top_outside'] = true
        # Loose panel: its thickness is one of the three sizes, so W × H × D is always the panel's outside.
        if p['panel']
          case p['panel_kind']
          when 'top', 'bottom' then p['height'] = p['panel_t']
          when 'side' then p['width'] = p['panel_t']
          else p['depth'] = p['panel_t']
          end
        end
        # Decorative side panels: inside the width unless "added to the width" is ticked.
        p['skin_add'] = p['skin_fit'] == 'add' unless input.key?('skin_add')
        p['skin_fit'] = p['skin_add'] ? 'add' : 'inside'
        p['back_type'] = if p['back_mount'] == 'applied' then 'applied'
                         elsif p['back_slot'] then 'groove'
                         else 'inset'
                         end

        cols = p['columns'].is_a?(Array) && !p['columns'].empty? ? p['columns'] : deep_copy(DEFAULTS['columns'])
        p['columns'] = cols.map do |c|
          c = {} unless c.is_a?(Hash)
          kind = c['kind'].to_s == 'kneehole' ? 'kneehole' : 'normal'
          rows = (c['rows'].is_a?(Array) ? c['rows'] : []).map do |r|
            r = {} unless r.is_a?(Hash)
            {
              'h' => size_spec(r['h']),
              'front' => FRONTS.include?(r['front'].to_s) ? r['front'].to_s : 'door',
              'hinge' => HINGES.include?(r['hinge'].to_s) ? r['hinge'].to_s : 'L',
              'interior' => INTERIORS.include?(r['interior'].to_s) ? r['interior'].to_s : 'none',
              'shelves' => [[num(r['shelves'], 0).to_i, 0].max, 12].min
            }.merge(split_of(r))
          end
          rows = [{ 'h' => 'auto', 'front' => 'none', 'hinge' => 'L', 'interior' => 'none', 'shelves' => 0 }] if rows.empty? && kind == 'normal'
          { 'w' => size_spec(c['w']), 'kind' => kind, 'rows' => rows }
        end
        if p['columns'].all? { |c| c['kind'] == 'kneehole' }
          p['columns'][0]['kind'] = 'normal'
          p['columns'][0]['rows'] = deep_copy(DEFAULTS['columns'][0]['rows'])
        end
        # NOOKS: the box as spaces split side by side or one above the other, as deep as wanted.
        # Stored only when that layout is chosen (other modules keep their codes).
        if p['layout_mode'].to_s == 'nooks'
          p['layout_mode'] = 'nooks'
          p['nooks'] = p['nooks'].is_a?(Hash) ? nook_norm(p['nooks'], 0) : nooks_from_columns(p['columns'])
        else
          p.delete('layout_mode')
          p['nooks'] = nook_norm(p['nooks'], 0) if p['nooks'].is_a?(Hash) # kept to come back to
        end
        p['name'] = p['name'].to_s.strip.empty? ? 'Module' : p['name'].to_s.strip
        p
      end

      # "Split below this row": stored only when ticked (with the lower box's top when it is not
      # the module's choice), so older modules keep their codes.
      def self.box_split_of(q)
        return {} unless q.is_a?(Hash)
        q = q.merge('split' => q['box_split']) if q.key?('box_split')
        s = split_of(q)
        s.empty? ? {} : { 'box_split' => true }.merge(s['split_top'] ? { 'split_top' => s['split_top'] } : {})
      end

      def self.split_of(r)
        return {} unless r['split'] == true || r['split'] == 'true'
        top = %w[stretchers full_panel].include?(r['split_top'].to_s) ? { 'split_top' => r['split_top'].to_s } : {}
        { 'split' => true }.merge(top)
      end

      NOOK_FRONTS = %w[none door door_pair drawer false_front].freeze
      NOOK_DEPTH = 8

      # A node: { 'split' => 'v' (side by side) | 'h' (one above the other), 'parts' => [node…] }
      # or a nook (leaf): { 'front', 'hinge', 'interior', 'shelves', 'drawers' }. Each part may
      # carry 'size' ('auto' or mm: clear width for 'v', clear height for 'h').
      def self.nook_norm(n, depth)
        n = {} unless n.is_a?(Hash)
        size = n.key?('size') ? size_spec(n['size']) : 'auto'
        if %w[v h].include?(n['split'].to_s) && n['parts'].is_a?(Array) && n['parts'].size >= 2 && depth < NOOK_DEPTH
          return { 'size' => size, 'split' => n['split'].to_s, 'parts' => n['parts'].map { |q| nook_norm(q, depth + 1).merge(box_split_of(q)) } }
        end
        n = n['parts'][0] if n['parts'].is_a?(Array) && n['parts'].size == 1 && n['parts'][0].is_a?(Hash)
        front = n['front'].to_s.sub(/\Aglass_/, '')
        {
          'size' => size,
          'front' => NOOK_FRONTS.include?(front) ? front : 'none',
          'hinge' => HINGES.include?(n['hinge'].to_s) ? n['hinge'].to_s : 'L',
          'interior' => INTERIORS.include?(n['interior'].to_s) ? n['interior'].to_s : 'none',
          'shelves' => [[num(n['shelves'], 0).to_i, 0].max, 12].min,
          'drawers' => [[num(n['drawers'], 1).to_i, 1].max, 8].min
        }
      end

      # Today's columns and rows as nooks: columns side by side, each split into its rows.
      def self.nooks_from_columns(cols)
        parts = (cols || []).reject { |c| c['kind'] == 'kneehole' }.map do |c|
          rows = c['rows'].map { |r| r.merge('size' => r['h'] == 'auto' ? 'auto' : r['h']).reject { |k, _| k == 'h' } }
          node = rows.size > 1 ? { 'split' => 'h', 'parts' => rows } : rows[0]
          node.merge('size' => c['w'])
        end
        root = parts.size > 1 ? { 'split' => 'v', 'parts' => parts } : (parts[0] || {})
        nook_norm(root.merge('size' => 'auto'), 0)
      end

      def self.nook_mirror(n)
        return n.merge('hinge' => { 'L' => 'R', 'R' => 'L' }[n['hinge']] || n['hinge']) unless n['parts']
        parts = n['parts'].map { |q| nook_mirror(q) }
        n.merge('parts' => n['split'] == 'v' ? parts.reverse : parts)
      end

      # Mirror left/right (used when the module is flipped with "Flip Along").
      # Stretching a blind corner module: keep the blind side as it is now and let
      # the door absorb the width change ("Set door width" becomes "Set blind width").
      # Fridge enclosure: module size around a fridge (sides, gaps, top cabinet).
      def self.fridge_fit(p)
        t = p['t'].to_f
        p.merge('width' => p['fridge_w'].to_f + 2 * p['fridge_gap_side'].to_f + 2 * t,
                'height' => p['fridge_h'].to_f + p['fridge_gap_top'].to_f + p['fridge_top_h'].to_f,
                'depth' => [p['fridge_d'].to_f, p['fridge_top_d'].to_f].max)
      end

      def self.keep_blind(p, corner)
        return p unless corner && p['corner'].to_s != 'none' && p['corner_size'] == 'door'
        p.merge('corner_size' => 'blind', 'corner_blind_w' => corner['blind_w'])
      end

      def self.mirrored(p)
        q = deep_copy(p)
        q['columns'] = q['columns'].reverse.map do |c|
          c['rows'].each { |r| r['hinge'] = { 'L' => 'R', 'R' => 'L' }[r['hinge']] || r['hinge'] }
          c
        end
        q['corner'] = { 'left' => 'right', 'right' => 'left' }[q['corner']] || q['corner']
        q['nooks'] = nook_mirror(q['nooks']) if q['nooks'].is_a?(Hash)
        q
      end
    end
  end
end

# encoding: UTF-8
# CSPARTNERS PANEL PRO — parametric module builder.
#
# Turns a parameter hash into a list of parts. No SketchUp API here, so it can be
# tested in plain Ruby. Coordinates are millimetres, module-local:
#   x = width  (left → right), origin at the left outer face
#   y = depth  (front → back), y = 0 is the front plane of the box (face frame front
#       in face-frame mode). Overlay fronts sit at y < 0.
#   z = height (floor → up), z = 0 is the floor / underside of the module.
#
# A "prism" part is a 2D profile in the plane perpendicular to `axis`, extruded
# `thk` from `pos` along that axis. Profile coordinates (u, v):
#   axis x → (y, z)   axis y → (x, z)   axis z → (x, y)

module CSPartners
  module PanelPro
    class BuildError < StandardError; end

    module Builder
      def self.build(params)
        p = Params.normalize(params)
        res = Split.wanted?(p) ? Split.build(p) : Run.new(p).build
        apply_edges(res, p['edges'])
      end

      # ------------------------------------------------------------------ split module
      # Rows (or the top-level NOOKS spaces) ticked "split below" cut the module into boxes
      # stacked on each other, each a complete carcass of its own. Each box is built by the
      # same builder with its own rows and height and moved up into place; the decorative
      # side / back panels and the decorative top come from the whole module. At each split
      # the lower box's top is stretchers (default) or a full panel, the upper box keeps its
      # full bottom. Boxes are numbered from the floor up; 'boxes' gives each one's settings
      # so it can be separated into a module of its own.
      module Split
        module_function

        def wanted?(p)
          if p['layout_mode'] == 'nooks'
            n = p['nooks']
            n.is_a?(Hash) && n['split'] == 'h' && n['parts'][0..-2].any? { |q| q['box_split'] }
          else
            p['columns'].any? { |c| c['rows'][0..-2].any? { |r| r['split'] } }
          end
        end

        def r(v)
          (v.to_f * 10).round / 10.0
        end

        def deep(o)
          Marshal.load(Marshal.dump(o))
        end

        def build(p)
          full = Run.new(p).build
          why = if p['panel'] || p['fridge'] then 'panels and fridge modules'
                elsif p['construction'] == 'face_frame' then 'face-frame modules'
                elsif p['corner'].to_s != 'none' && !p['corner'].to_s.empty? then 'corner modules'
                elsif p['layout_mode'] != 'nooks' && p['columns'].any? { |c| c['kind'] == 'kneehole' } then 'modules with a kneehole'
                end
          if why
            full['warnings'] << "Split module: not available for #{why} — built as one box."
            return full
          end
          cuts = p['layout_mode'] == 'nooks' ? nook_cuts(p, full) : row_cuts(p, full)
          return full if cuts.empty?
          h = p['height'].to_f
          zs = [0.0] + cuts.map { |c| c['z'] } + [h]   # box bottoms / tops, floor up
          n = zs.size - 1
          res = { 'parts' => [], 'warnings' => full['warnings'].dup, 'hardware' => [], 'movers' => [],
                  'corner' => nil, 'layout' => full['layout'], 'staircase' => false, 'nooks' => full['nooks'],
                  'bbox' => full['bbox'], 'params' => p, 'boxes' => [] }
          hw = Hash.new(0)
          n.times do |i|
            z0 = zs[i]
            z1 = zs[i + 1]
            q = box_params(p, full, i, n, z0, z1, i.zero? ? nil : cuts[i - 1], i == n - 1 ? nil : cuts[i])
            run = Run.new(q)
            sub = run.build
            run.shift_all(0, 0, z0)
            pre = "B#{i + 1}:"
            sub['parts'].each do |pt|
              next if %w[skin top].include?(pt['role'])   # from the whole module (below)
              pt['pid'] = pre + pt['pid'].to_s
              pt['box'] = i + 1
              pt['mover'] = pre + pt['mover'] if pt['mover']
              pt['hinge_of'] = pre + pt['hinge_of'] if pt['hinge_of']
              pt['slide_of'] = pre + pt['slide_of'] if pt['slide_of']
              pt['hinge'] = pt['hinge'].merge('door' => pre + pt['hinge']['door'].to_s) if pt['hinge'].is_a?(Hash) && pt['hinge']['door']
              pt['slide'] = pt['slide'].merge('drawer' => pre + pt['slide']['drawer'].to_s) if pt['slide'].is_a?(Hash) && pt['slide']['drawer']
              res['parts'] << pt
            end
            sub['movers'].each { |m| res['movers'] << m.merge('id' => pre + m['id'].to_s, 'box' => i + 1) }
            sub['hardware'].each { |item, k| hw[item] += k }
            sub['warnings'].each { |w| res['warnings'] << w unless res['warnings'].include?(w) }
            res['staircase'] ||= sub['staircase']
            sp = deep(q)
            sp['name'] = "#{p['name']} #{i + 1}"
            sp['elevation'] = r(p['elevation'].to_f + z0)
            sp['edges'] = (p['edges'] || {}).each_with_object({}) { |(k, v), o| o[k.sub(pre, '')] = v if k.start_with?(pre) }
            sp.delete('edges') if sp['edges'].empty?
            res['boxes'] << { 'n' => i + 1, 'z' => r(z0), 'h' => r(z1 - z0), 'params' => sp }
          end
          full['parts'].each { |pt| res['parts'] << pt if %w[skin top].include?(pt['role']) }
          res['hardware'] = hw.to_a
          res
        end

        # Splits between rows: a row ticked "split below" in any column, where every column
        # has a row boundary at that height. → [{ 'z', 'top' }] floor up
        def row_cuts(p, full)
          h = p['height'].to_f
          bounds = full['layout'].map do |lc|
            acc = h
            (lc['rows'] || []).map { |rh| acc -= rh.to_f }
          end
          want = {}
          p['columns'].each_with_index do |c, ci|
            c['rows'][0..-2].each_with_index do |rw, ri|
              next unless rw['split']
              z = bounds[ci][ri]
              key = z.round
              want[key] ||= { 'z' => z, 'top' => rw['split_top'] }
            end
          end
          out = []
          want.values.sort_by { |c| c['z'] }.each do |c|
            if bounds.all? { |b| b[0..-2].any? { |z| (z - c['z']).abs <= 1.0 } }
              out << c
            else
              full['warnings'] << "Split module: the rows of every column must end at #{r c['z']} mm to split there — that split is left out."
            end
          end
          out
        end

        # Splits between the top-level NOOKS spaces (one above the other): halfway through the
        # panel between them.
        def nook_cuts(p, full)
          zs = (full['nooks'] || {})['root_cuts'] || []
          parts = p['nooks']['parts']
          out = []
          parts[0..-2].each_with_index do |q, i|
            out << { 'z' => zs[i], 'top' => q['split_top'], 'nook' => i } if q['box_split'] && zs[i]
          end
          out.sort_by { |c| c['z'] }
        end

        # The settings of box i (floor up) of n, from z0 to z1.
        def box_params(p, full, i, n, z0, z1, below, above)
          q = deep(p)
          q.delete('edges')
          q['height'] = r(z1 - z0)
          bottom = i.zero?
          top = i == n - 1
          unless bottom
            q['kick_type'] = 'none'
            q.delete('back_floor')
            q['end_bottom'] = false
          end
          unless top
            q['top_type'] = (above && above['top']) || p['split_top'] || 'stretchers'
            q['add_top'] = false
            q['ct_clear'] = false
            q['end_top'] = false
            %w[back_hset back_h back_over].each { |k| q.delete(k) }
          end
          if p['layout_mode'] == 'nooks'
            parts = p['nooks']['parts']
            lo = above ? above['nook'] + 1 : 0
            hi = below ? below['nook'] : parts.size - 1
            sub = deep(parts[lo..hi]).each { |x| x.delete('box_split'); x.delete('split_top') }
            sub.max_by { |x| x['size'] == 'auto' ? 1e9 : x['size'].to_f }['size'] = 'auto' unless sub.any? { |x| x['size'] == 'auto' }
            q['nooks'] = sub.size == 1 ? sub[0].merge('size' => 'auto') : { 'size' => 'auto', 'split' => 'h', 'parts' => sub }
          else
            h = p['height'].to_f
            q['columns'] = p['columns'].each_with_index.map do |c, ci|
              hs = full['layout'][ci]['rows']
              acc = h
              rows = []
              c['rows'].each_with_index do |rw, ri|
                top_z = acc
                acc -= hs[ri].to_f
                mid = (top_z + acc) / 2.0
                next unless mid > z0 && mid < z1
                x = rw.reject { |k, _| %w[split split_top].include?(k) }
                x['h'] = r(hs[ri]) unless rw['h'] == 'auto'
                rows << x
              end
              c.merge('rows' => rows)
            end
          end
          Params.normalize(q)
        end
      end

      SIDES = %w[L1 L2 W1 W2].freeze

      # Edge banding the builder gives a part: { 'L1' => true, … } from its 'eb' count.
      def self.eb_flags(eb)
        l_n = eb.to_s[/(\d)L/, 1].to_i
        w_n = eb.to_s[/(\d)W/, 1].to_i
        { 'L1' => l_n >= 1, 'L2' => l_n >= 2, 'W1' => w_n >= 1, 'W2' => w_n >= 2 }
      end

      # '1010' (L1 L2 W1 W2) ↔ flags
      def self.flags_code(fl)
        SIDES.map { |k| fl[k] ? '1' : '0' }.join
      end

      def self.code_flags(code)
        c = code.to_s
        { 'L1' => c[0] == '1', 'L2' => c[1] == '1', 'W1' => c[2] == '1', 'W2' => c[3] == '1' }
      end

      def self.flags_eb(fl)
        l_n = (fl['L1'] ? 1 : 0) + (fl['L2'] ? 1 : 0)
        w_n = (fl['W1'] ? 1 : 0) + (fl['W2'] ? 1 : 0)
        [l_n > 0 ? "#{l_n}L" : nil, w_n > 0 ? "#{w_n}W" : nil].compact.join(' ')
      end

      # Edge banding chosen by hand in the cut list (params 'edges' = { pid => '1010' }).
      # Every cut part gets 'edges' (per side); overridden ones also get a new 'eb'.
      def self.apply_edges(res, over)
        over = {} unless over.is_a?(Hash)
        res['parts'].each do |pt|
          next unless pt['cut']
          code = over[pt['pid'].to_s]
          if code.is_a?(String) && code =~ /\A[01]{4}\z/
            fl = code_flags(code)
            pt['edges'] = fl
            pt['eb'] = flags_eb(fl)
            pt['eb_set'] = true
          else
            pt['edges'] = eb_flags(pt['eb'])
          end
        end
        res
      end

      class Run
        def initialize(p)
          @p = p
          @parts = []
          @warnings = []
          @hw = {}
          @movers = []
          @drawer_n = 0
        end

        def build
          return build_panel if @p['panel']
          return build_fridge if @p['fridge']
          setup
          layout_columns
          layout_rows
          nooks_layout if @nooks
          carcass
          base
          worktop
          face_frame if @ff
          setup_corner
          contents
          nooks_contents if @nooks
          corner_parts
          skins
          visible_faces
          shift_x(@sl) if @skin_in && @sl > 0
          assign_pids
          {
            'parts' => @parts,
            'warnings' => @warnings,
            'hardware' => @hw.to_a,
            'movers' => @movers,
            'corner' => @cn && { 'blind_w' => r(@cn['blind_w']), 'opening' => r(@cn['opening']) },
            'layout' => layout_summary,
            'staircase' => staircase_drawers,
            'nooks' => @nooks ? nooks_summary : nil,
            'bbox' => bbox,
            'params' => @p
          }
        end

        # ------------------------------------------------------------------ fridge enclosure
        # Two tall sides on the floor, a cabinet of its own nested between them at the top
        # (front flush with the sides' front edge, built with this module's fronts and
        # layout), and optionally a back behind the fridge. Opening = width − 2 sides,
        # height − top cabinet.
        def build_fridge
          t = f('t'); w = f('width'); h = f('height'); d = f('depth')
          raise BuildError, 'Panel thickness must be greater than zero.' if t <= 0
          th = f('fridge_top_h'); td = [[f('fridge_top_d'), 100.0].max, d].min
          raise BuildError, "Fridge module: the top cabinet (#{fmt th} mm) leaves no room for the fridge — make the module taller." if th >= h - 300
          raise BuildError, 'Fridge module: too narrow for two sides and a top cabinet.' if w - 2 * t < 150
          top = @p.merge('fridge' => false, 'width' => w - 2 * t, 'height' => th, 'depth' => td, 'elevation' => 0,
                         'kick_type' => 'none', 'corner' => 'none', 'skin_l' => false, 'skin_r' => false,
                         'end_l' => false, 'end_r' => false, 'add_top' => false, 'top_type' => 'full_panel')
          sub = Run.new(Params.normalize(top)).build
          @parts = sub['parts']
          @movers = sub['movers']
          shift_all(t, 0.0, h - th)
          sub['warnings'].each { |m| warn(m) }
          sub['hardware'].each { |i, q| hw(i, q) }
          mc = s('mat_carcass')
          # a visible side (Visible end panels) takes the end-panel material, like any module
          [[@p['end_l'], 0, t], [@p['end_r'], w - t, w]].each do |vis, x0, x1|
            note = vis ? 'fridge enclosure, on the floor; visible end' : 'fridge enclosure, on the floor'
            panel('Tall side', 'carcass', vis ? s('mat_end') : mc, x0, x1, 0, d, 0, h, 'x', 'z', '1L 1W', 'note' => note)
          end
          if s('fridge_back') == 'full'
            bt = f('back_t')
            panel('Back (fridge)', 'back', s('mat_back'), t, w - t, d - bt, d, 0, h, 'y', 'z', '', 'note' => 'behind the fridge, between the tall sides')
          end
          ow = w - 2 * t
          oh = h - th
          assign_pids
          { 'parts' => @parts, 'warnings' => @warnings, 'hardware' => @hw.to_a, 'movers' => @movers,
            'corner' => nil, 'fridge' => { 'opening_w' => r(ow), 'opening_h' => r(oh) }, 'layout' => sub['layout'],
            'bbox' => bbox, 'params' => @p }
        end

        # ------------------------------------------------------------------ loose panel
        # One panel on its own, placed and stretched like a module: a top (overpanel) lying over
        # several modules, an end panel standing beside them, a filler closing a gap at the front,
        # or a back cover. W × H × D is the panel's outside; the thickness is one of them.
        PANEL_NAMES = { 'top' => 'Overpanel', 'bottom' => 'Underpanel', 'side' => 'End panel', 'filler' => 'Filler',
                        'back' => 'Back cover', 'crown' => 'Crown' }.freeze
        PANEL_EB = { 'front' => '1L', 'long' => '2L', 'all' => '2L 2W', 'none' => '' }.freeze
        def build_panel
          t = f('panel_t'); w = f('width'); h = f('height'); d = f('depth')
          raise BuildError, 'Panel thickness must be greater than zero.' if t <= 0
          kind = s('panel_kind')
          name = PANEL_NAMES[kind]
          eb = PANEL_EB[s('panel_eb')] || ''
          mat = %w[top bottom].include?(kind) ? s('mat_top') : s('mat_skin')
          case kind
          when 'top', 'bottom' then panel(name, 'skin', mat, 0, w, 0, d, 0, t, 'z', 'x', eb)
          when 'crown' then panel(name, 'skin', mat, 0, w, 0, t, 0, h, 'y', 'x', eb)
          when 'side' then panel(name, 'skin', mat, 0, t, 0, d, 0, h, 'x', 'z', eb)
          else panel(name, 'skin', mat, 0, w, 0, t, 0, h, 'y', w >= h ? 'x' : 'z', eb)
          end
          assign_pids
          { 'parts' => @parts, 'warnings' => @warnings, 'hardware' => @hw.to_a, 'movers' => @movers,
            'corner' => nil, 'layout' => [], 'bbox' => bbox, 'params' => @p }
        end

        # Drawers opened for show: in each column the top drawer comes out least and each one
        # below a little further (35 % … 65 % of its pull-out), like a staircase.
        STAIR_LO = 0.35
        STAIR_HI = 0.65
        def staircase_drawers
          return false unless s('drawer_open') == 'staircase'
          @movers.select { |m| m['kind'] == 'drawer' && m['at'] }.group_by { |m| m['tag'].to_s[/\A[CN]\d+/] }.each_value do |list|
            list = list.sort_by { |m| -m['at'][1] }
            n = list.size
            list.each_with_index do |m, i|
              frac = n == 1 ? 0.5 : STAIR_LO + (STAIR_HI - STAIR_LO) * i / (n - 1)
              m['travel'] = r(m['travel'].to_f * frac)
            end
          end
          true
        end

        # What 'auto' came out as: each column's clear width and each row's section height
        # (the same measures the Layout tab takes), for the Configurator to show.
        def layout_summary
          (@cols || []).map do |c|
            { 'w' => r(c['x1'] - c['x0']), 'rows' => (c['hs'] || []).map { |h| r(h) } }
          end
        end

        # Move every part (and door / drawer pivots) by (dx, dy, dz) mm.
        def shift_all(dx, dy, dz)
          dv = { 'x' => dx, 'y' => dy, 'z' => dz }
          @parts.each do |pt|
            if pt['shape'] == 'cyl'
              pt['center'] = [pt['center'][0] + dx, pt['center'][1] + dy, pt['center'][2] + dz].map { |v| r(v) }
            else
              u, v = plane_axes(pt['axis'])
              pt['pos'] = r(pt['pos'] + dv[pt['axis']])
              pt['pts'] = pt['pts'].map { |q| [r(q[0] + dv[u]), r(q[1] + dv[v])] }
              (pt['grooves'] || []).each { |ln| ln.each { |q| q[0] = r(q[0] + dv[u]); q[1] = r(q[1] + dv[v]) } }
            end
            if (sl = pt['slide'])
              sl['face_x'] = r(sl['face_x'] + dx); sl['y'] = r(sl['y'] + dy); sl['zc'] = r(sl['zc'] + dz)
            end
            if (hg = pt['hinge'])
              hg['x'] = r(hg['x'] + dx); hg['y'] = r(hg['y'] + dy); hg['z'] = r(hg['z'] + dz)
              hg['side_x'] = r(hg['side_x'] + dx) if hg['side_x']
            end
          end
          @movers.each do |m|
            m['pivot'] = [m['pivot'][0] + dx, m['pivot'][1] + dy, m['pivot'][2] + dz].map { |v| r(v) } if m['pivot']
            m['at'] = [r(m['at'][0] + dx), r(m['at'][1] + dz)] if m['at']
          end
        end

        # Stable id per part ("Side|", "Door|C1R2|0", "Adj. shelf|C1R1|1") so a
        # rebuild can find the same physical panel again (hand-painted materials).
        def assign_pids
          seen = Hash.new(0)
          @parts.each do |pt|
            k = "#{pt['name']}|#{pt['tag']}"
            pt['pid'] = "#{k}|#{seen[k]}"
            seen[k] += 1
          end
        end

        # ------------------------------------------------------------------ helpers
        def f(k); @p[k].to_f; end
        def s(k); @p[k].to_s; end
        def r(v); (v.to_f * 10).round / 10.0; end

        def fmt(v)
          v = r(v)
          v == v.to_i ? v.to_i.to_s : v.to_s
        end

        def warn(m); @warnings << m unless @warnings.include?(m); end

        def hw(item, qty)
          return if qty <= 0
          @hw[item] = (@hw[item] || 0) + qty
        end

        def plane_axes(axis)
          case axis
          when 'x' then %w[y z]
          when 'y' then %w[x z]
          else %w[x y]
          end
        end

        # Generic extruded part.
        def prism(name, role, mat, axis, pos, thk, pts, grain, eb, extra = {})
          u, v = plane_axes(axis)
          pts = pts.map { |q| [r(q[0]), r(q[1])] } # round first so cut sizes == drawn sizes
          thk = r(thk)
          us = pts.map { |q| q[0] }
          vs = pts.map { |q| q[1] }
          du = us.max - us.min
          dv = vs.max - vs.min
          if du < 1 || dv < 1 || thk < 0.5
            warn("Skipped '#{name}': it came out too small (#{fmt du}×#{fmt dv}×#{fmt thk} mm).")
            return nil
          end
          # Cut-list length follows the longer side for box parts (edge banding is
          # given per physical edge, so the L/W counts swap with it).
          if pts.size >= 4 && AUTO_GRAIN_ROLES.include?(role) && s('grain_rule') == 'longest'
            along, across = grain == u ? [du, dv] : [dv, du]
            if across > along + 0.05
              grain = grain == u ? v : u
              eb = swap_eb(eb)
            end
          end
          len, wid = grain == u ? [du, dv] : [dv, du]
          part = {
            'name' => name, 'role' => role, 'mat' => mat, 'shape' => 'prism',
            'axis' => axis, 'pos' => r(pos), 'thk' => r(thk),
            'pts' => pts.map { |q| [r(q[0]), r(q[1])] },
            'L' => r(len), 'W' => r(wid), 'T' => r(thk), 'grain' => grain, 'eb' => eb, 'cut' => true
          }
          part.merge!(extra)
          @parts << part
          part
        end

        AUTO_GRAIN_ROLES = %w[carcass shelf back drawer base skin].freeze

        # '1L' ↔ '1W', '2L 1W' ↔ '1L 2W' …
        def swap_eb(eb)
          l_n = eb.to_s[/(\d)L/, 1].to_i
          w_n = eb.to_s[/(\d)W/, 1].to_i
          [w_n > 0 ? "#{w_n}L" : nil, l_n > 0 ? "#{l_n}W" : nil].compact.join(' ')
        end

        # Axis-aligned rectangular panel. `thin` is the thickness axis, `grain` the
        # in-plane axis that the grain (cut-list length) runs along.
        def panel(name, role, mat, x0, x1, y0, y1, z0, z1, thin, grain, eb = '', extra = {})
          lo = { 'x' => x0, 'y' => y0, 'z' => z0 }
          hi = { 'x' => x1, 'y' => y1, 'z' => z1 }
          u, v = plane_axes(thin)
          pts = [[lo[u], lo[v]], [hi[u], lo[v]], [hi[u], hi[v]], [lo[u], hi[v]]]
          prism(name, role, mat, thin, lo[thin], hi[thin] - lo[thin], pts, grain, eb, extra)
        end

        def cyl(name, mat, center, axis, radius, length, extra = {})
          part = {
            'name' => name, 'role' => 'hardware', 'mat' => mat, 'shape' => 'cyl',
            'center' => center.map { |c| r(c) }, 'axis' => axis, 'r' => radius, 'len' => r(length), 'cut' => false
          }
          part.merge!(extra)
          @parts << part
        end

        def hardware_box(name, x0, x1, y0, y1, z0, z1, thin, extra = {})
          panel(name, 'hardware', Params::METAL, x0, x1, y0, y1, z0, z1, thin, thin == 'z' ? 'x' : 'y', '', extra.merge('cut' => false))
        end

        # A moving assembly (door or drawer). Parts carry its id in 'mover'.
        # pivot/axis/angle describe the open position for doors (module-local mm,
        # degrees, right-hand rule); travel is the pull-out distance for drawers.
        def add_mover(h)
          @movers << h
          h['id']
        end

        # Split `total` between fixed sizes and 'auto' entries.
        def distribute(specs, total, label)
          fixed = specs.select { |x| x.is_a?(Numeric) }
          fixed_sum = fixed.inject(0.0) { |a, b| a + b }
          autos = specs.size - fixed.size
          if autos > 0
            aw = (total - fixed_sum) / autos
            raise BuildError, "Fixed #{label} (#{fmt fixed_sum} mm) leave no room for the 'auto' ones — only #{fmt total} mm available." if aw < 20
            specs.map { |x| x.is_a?(Numeric) ? x.to_f : aw }
          else
            scale = total / fixed_sum
            warn("#{label.capitalize} (#{fmt fixed_sum} mm) were scaled to fit the #{fmt total} mm available — set one to 'auto' to control this.") if (fixed_sum - total).abs > 0.5
            specs.map { |x| x * scale }
          end
        end

        # ------------------------------------------------------------------ setup
        def setup
          # Decorative side panels: inside the given width (carcass narrows) or added to it.
          @sl = @p['skin_l'] ? f('skin_t') : 0.0
          @sr = @p['skin_r'] ? f('skin_t') : 0.0
          @skin_in = s('skin_fit') == 'inside'
          @W = f('width') - (@skin_in ? @sl + @sr : 0.0); @H = f('height'); @D = f('depth')
          @t = f('t'); @ft = f('front_t'); @gap = f('gap'); @rev = f('reveal')
          raise BuildError, 'Panel thickness must be greater than zero.' if @t <= 0

          @ff = s('construction') == 'face_frame'
          @fft = @ff ? f('ff_t') : 0.0
          @ffov = @ff ? f('ff_overhang') : 0.0
          @st = f('ff_stile'); @rail = f('ff_rail'); @mid = f('ff_mid')
          @ffo = f('ff_overlay'); @ffg = f('ff_inset_gap')
          @cx0 = @ffov; @cx1 = @W - @ffov; @cy0 = @fft

          @nooks = s('layout_mode') == 'nooks' && @p['nooks'].is_a?(Hash)
          if @nooks && s('corner') != 'none' && !s('corner').empty?
            warn('NOOKS are not used on corner modules — the columns and rows are used.')
            @nooks = false
          end
          has_knee = !@nooks && @p['columns'].any? { |c| c['kind'] == 'kneehole' }
          @joint = s('joint')
          # sides_full: sides run down past the bottom, top between them; top_full: same, but the
          # top lies over the sides; bottom_full: bottom under the sides; top_bottom_full: both over
          @sides_low = %w[sides_full top_full].include?(@joint)
          @top_over = %w[top_bottom_full top_full].include?(@joint)
          @kick = s('kick_type')
          @kh = @kick == 'none' ? 0.0 : f('kick_h')
          if has_knee && !@sides_low
            warn('Kneehole layouts are built with sides over the bottom (sides full height).')
            @joint = @top_over ? 'top_full' : 'sides_full'
            @sides_low = true
          end
          if @kick == 'integral' && !@sides_low
            warn('A notched (integral) toe kick needs sides that run to the floor — a separate plinth is used instead.')
            @kick = 'plinth'
          end

          # The module height is the carcass. A decorative top sits on it, outside the height.
          @add_top = @p['add_top']
          @top = @H
          @top_t = @add_top ? f('top_t') : 0.0
          @base_z = @kh
          @bottom_under = @base_z + (@ff ? [@rail - @t, 0.0].max : 0.0)
          @bottom_top = @bottom_under + @t

          @stretch = s('top_type') == 'stretchers'
          # Front and rear stretchers each flat or on edge, each with its own width.
          @on_edge = s('front_stretcher_orient') == 'on_edge'
          @r_on_edge = s('rear_stretcher_orient') == 'on_edge'
          @sw = f('stretcher_w')
          @rsw = f('rear_stretcher_w')
          @drop = @stretch ? f('stretcher_drop') : 0.0
          front_h = @on_edge ? @sw : @t
          rear_h = @p['rear_stretcher'] ? (@r_on_edge ? @rsw : @t) : 0.0
          @top_under = @stretch ? @top - [front_h, rear_h].max : @top - @t
          @top_edge = @stretch ? @drop + front_h : @t

          @back = s('back_type'); @bt = f('back_t'); @g = f('groove_depth')
          rec = @back == 'applied' ? 0.0 : f('back_recess')
          @y_back_rear = @D - rec
          @y_back_front = @y_back_rear - @bt
          @y_tb_back = case @back
                       when 'groove' then @D
                       when 'inset' then @y_back_rear
                       else @D - @bt
                       end
          @side_back = @back == 'applied' ? @D - @bt : @D

          if @back == 'groove'
            warn("Back groove is #{fmt @g} mm deep in #{fmt @t} mm panels — keep it under half the thickness.") if @g > @t / 2.0 + 0.05
            warn("Back groove is only #{fmt rec} mm from the rear edge — that lip may break out.") if rec < 6
          end

          @overlay = s('overlay')
          @inset = @overlay == 'inset'
          @y_int_front = @inset ? [@cy0, @ft].max : @cy0
          @notch = [f('kick_setback'), @t].max
          @divider = s('row_divider') == 'fixed_shelf'
          @knee_all = s('knee_sides') == 'all'
          @ct_drop = @p['ct_clear'] ? [f('ct_clear_mm'), 0.0].max : 0.0

          @mc = s('mat_carcass'); @mb = s('mat_back'); @mf = s('mat_front'); @mff = s('mat_frame')
          @md = s('mat_drawer'); @mt = s('mat_top'); @mk = s('mat_kick')

          raise BuildError, "Height is too small: the box interior would be #{fmt(@top_under - @bottom_top)} mm." if @top_under - @bottom_top < 60
          raise BuildError, "Depth is too small: only #{fmt(@y_back_front - @cy0)} mm in front of the back panel." if @y_back_front - @cy0 < 60
          raise BuildError, 'Width is too small for two side panels.' if @cx1 - @cx0 < 2 * @t + 40
        end

        # ------------------------------------------------------------------ layout
        def layout_columns
          # NOOKS: one column the full width; the nooks fill it (nooks_layout)
          specs = @nooks ? [{ 'w' => 'auto', 'kind' => 'normal', 'rows' => [] }] : @p['columns']
          n = specs.size
          inner0 = @cx0 + @t
          inner1 = @cx1 - @t
          avail = inner1 - inner0 - (n - 1) * @t
          raise BuildError, "Module too narrow for #{n} columns." if avail < 40 * n
          widths = distribute(specs.map { |c| c['w'] }, avail, 'column widths')
          x = inner0
          @cols = []
          specs.each_with_index do |c, i|
            w = widths[i]
            @cols << { 'i' => i, 'x0' => x, 'x1' => x + w, 'kind' => c['kind'], 'rows' => c['rows'],
                       'first' => i.zero?, 'last' => i == n - 1, 'tag' => "C#{i + 1}" }
            x += w + @t
          end
          @cols.each_with_index do |c, i|
            c['cl'] = i.zero? ? nil : @cols[i - 1]['x1'] + @t / 2.0
            c['cr'] = i == n - 1 ? nil : c['x1'] + @t / 2.0
            c['knee'] = c['kind'] == 'kneehole'
          end
          # Segments = runs of normal columns (kneeholes split bottoms, backs and kicks).
          @segs = []
          @cols.each do |c|
            next if c['knee']
            if @segs.empty? || @segs.last['c1'] != c['i'] - 1
              @segs << { 'x0' => c['x0'], 'x1' => c['x1'], 'c0' => c['i'], 'c1' => c['i'] }
            else
              @segs.last['x1'] = c['x1']
              @segs.last['c1'] = c['i']
            end
          end
        end

        def layout_rows
          zlo = @ff ? @base_z : @bottom_under
          zhi = @top
          @cols.each do |c|
            next if c['knee']
            rows = c['rows']
            if rows.empty?
              c['hs'] = []
              c['slots'] = []
              next
            end
            hs = distribute(rows.map { |rw| rw['h'] }, zhi - zlo, "row heights in column #{c['i'] + 1}")
            c['hs'] = hs
            z1 = zhi
            c['slots'] = rows.each_with_index.map do |rw, j|
              z0 = j == rows.size - 1 ? zlo : z1 - hs[j]
              sl = { 'row' => rw, 'z0' => z0, 'z1' => z1, 'first' => j.zero?, 'last' => j == rows.size - 1,
                     'tag' => "#{c['tag']}R#{j + 1}" }
              sl['iz0'] = sl['last'] ? @bottom_top : z0 + (@divider ? @t / 2.0 : 0)
              sl['iz1'] = sl['first'] ? @top_under : z1 - (@divider ? @t / 2.0 : 0)
              z1 = z0
              sl
            end
          end
        end

        # ------------------------------------------------------------------ carcass
        # floor: the panel runs to the floor whatever the base (kneehole sides).
        # end_panel: a desk end beside a kneehole — no cabinet above, so no toe-kick notch.
        def upright(name, x0, x1, inner = false, floor = false, end_panel = false)
          z0 = if floor then 0.0
               elsif @sides_low
                 %w[integral none].include?(@kick) ? 0.0 : @base_z
               else
                 @bottom_top
               end
          z1 = if inner then @top_under
               elsif @top_over && !@stretch then @top - @t
               else @top
               end
          y0 = @cy0
          y1 = @side_back
          notched = !end_panel && @sides_low && @kick == 'integral' && @kh > 0 && @notch > y0 + 0.5
          pts = if notched
                  [[y0, @kh], [@notch, @kh], [@notch, 0.0], [y1, 0.0], [y1, z1], [y0, z1]]
                else
                  [[y0, z0], [y1, z0], [y1, z1], [y0, z1]]
                end
          extra = notched ? { 'note' => "toe-kick notch #{fmt(@notch - y0)}×#{fmt @kh}" } : {}
          # A visible end (no decorative panel over it) takes the end-panel material.
          mat = @mc
          if (name == 'Side L' && @p['end_l'] && @sl <= 0) || (name == 'Side R' && @p['end_r'] && @sr <= 0)
            mat = s('mat_end')
            extra = extra.merge('note' => [extra['note'], 'visible end'].compact.join('; '))
          end
          prism(name, 'carcass', mat, 'x', x0, x1 - x0, pts, 'z', '1L 1W', extra)  # front edge + one end
        end

        def carcass
          # A side that closes a kneehole at the end of a desk stands on the floor.
          upright('Side L', @cx0, @cx0 + @t, false, @cols.first['knee'], @cols.first['knee'])
          upright('Side R', @cx1 - @t, @cx1, false, @cols.last['knee'], @cols.last['knee'])

          # Partitions between columns
          @cols.each_with_index do |c, i|
            next if c['last']
            nb = @cols[i + 1]
            px0 = c['x1']
            px1 = c['x1'] + @t
            if c['knee'] || nb['knee']
              upright('Pedestal side', px0, px1, true, @knee_all)
            else
              panel('Partition', 'carcass', @mc, px0, px1, @cy0, @y_back_front, @bottom_top, @top_under, 'x', 'z', '1L')
            end
          end

          # Bottom(s)
          if @sides_low
            @segs.each do |sg|
              panel('Bottom', 'carcass', @mc, sg['x0'], sg['x1'], @cy0, @y_tb_back, @bottom_under, @bottom_top, 'z', 'x', '1L')
            end
          else
            panel('Bottom', 'carcass', @mc, @cx0, @cx1, @cy0, @y_tb_back, @bottom_under, @bottom_top, 'z', 'x', '1L')
          end

          # Top / stretchers
          if @stretch
            sx0 = @cx0 + @t
            sx1 = @cx1 - @t
            fy = @cy0 + f('stretcher_setback')
            if @on_edge
              panel('Front stretcher', 'carcass', @mc, sx0, sx1, fy, fy + @t, @top - @drop - @sw, @top - @drop, 'y', 'x', '1L')
            else
              panel('Front stretcher', 'carcass', @mc, sx0, sx1, fy, fy + @sw, @top - @drop - @t, @top - @drop, 'z', 'x', '1L')
            end
            if @p['rear_stretcher']
              if @r_on_edge
                panel('Rear stretcher', 'carcass', @mc, sx0, sx1, @y_back_front - @t, @y_back_front, @top - @rsw, @top, 'y', 'x', '1L')
              else
                panel('Rear stretcher', 'carcass', @mc, sx0, sx1, @y_back_front - @rsw, @y_back_front, @top - @t, @top, 'z', 'x', '1L')
              end
            end
          else
            tx0, tx1 = @top_over ? [@cx0, @cx1] : [@cx0 + @t, @cx1 - @t]
            panel('Top', 'carcass', @mc, tx0, tx1, @cy0, @y_tb_back, @top - @t, @top, 'z', 'x', '1L')
          end

          # Back(s)
          multi = @segs.size > 1
          @segs.each_with_index do |sg, i|
            nm = multi ? "Back #{i + 1}" : 'Back'
            case @back
            when 'groove'
              ztop = @stretch ? @top : @top_under + @g
              gw = [f('back_groove_w'), @bt].min
              note = "slotted: #{fmt gw} wide × #{fmt @g} deep groove, #{fmt(@D - @y_back_rear)} mm from rear"
              note += "; rebate edges to #{fmt gw} mm tongue" if @bt > gw + 0.05
              panel(nm, 'back', @mb, sg['x0'] - @g, sg['x1'] + @g, @y_back_front, @y_back_rear,
                    @bottom_top - @g, ztop, 'y', 'z', '', 'note' => note)
            when 'inset'
              ztop = @stretch ? @top : @top_under
              panel(nm, 'back', @mb, sg['x0'], sg['x1'], @y_back_front, @y_back_rear, @bottom_top, ztop, 'y', 'z', '',
                    'note' => "not slotted: set in between panels, #{fmt(@D - @y_back_rear)} mm from rear")
            else
              if @sides_low
                ax0 = sg['x0'] - @t
                ax1 = sg['x1'] + @t
              else
                ax0 = @cx0
                ax1 = @cx1
              end
              zb, zt = applied_back_z
              note = ['applied to rear', @p['back_floor'] ? 'to the floor' : nil, zt > @top + 0.05 ? "#{fmt(zt - @top)} mm above the module" : nil].compact.join('; ')
              panel(nm, 'back', @mb, ax0, ax1, @y_back_front, @y_back_rear, zb, zt, 'y', 'z', '2L 2W', 'note' => note)  # applied: all edges show
            end
          end

          # Modesty panels in kneeholes
          mh = f('modesty_h')
          @cols.each do |c|
            next unless c['knee'] && mh > 0
            z0 = [@top_under - mh, @base_z].max
            panel('Modesty panel', 'carcass', @mc, c['x0'], c['x1'], @y_back_rear - @t, @y_back_rear, z0, @top_under, 'y', 'x', '1L')
          end
        end

        # ------------------------------------------------------------------ base
        def base
