# encoding: UTF-8
# CSPARTNERS PANEL PRO — sheet optimizer (beam-saw / guillotine layouts). Pure Ruby.
#
# Cuts the way a beam saw such as a Biesse Sektor does with "Corte Largo":
#   1. rip full-length strips across the sheet width,
#   2. cross-cut each strip into segments,
#   3. split a segment into stacked parts of the same or shorter length.
# Every cut runs edge to edge, so the layouts can be cut on a panel saw too.
#
# Coordinates on a sheet: x along the sheet length (grain), y across its width,
# millimetres from the sheet corner (the trim is included in x/y).

module CSPartners
  module PanelPro
    module Optimizer
      SEARCH_SECONDS = 1.0
      MAX_TRIES = 400
      MAX_WIDTHS = 8
      MAX_HEADS = 24
      BIG_TYPES = 40

      DEFAULTS = { 'kerf' => 4.4, 'trim' => 10.0, 'sheet_l' => 2440.0, 'sheet_w' => 1220.0, 'tape_extra' => 10.0 }.freeze

      Item = Struct.new(:l, :w, :code, :part, :mod, :edges, :id)

      def self.fmt(v)
        v = (v.to_f * 10).round / 10.0
        v == v.to_i ? v.to_i.to_s : v.to_s
      end

      # rows:   cut-list rows (Cutlist.compile['rows'])
      # boards: material => { 'L', 'W' } (board library)
      # opts:   'kerf', 'trim', 'sheet_l', 'sheet_w', 'rotate' => { "material|T" => true }
      def self.run(rows, boards = {}, opts = {})
        o = DEFAULTS.merge(opts.reject { |_, v| v.nil? })
        kerf = o['kerf'].to_f
        trim = o['trim'].to_f
        rotate = o['rotate'] || {}
        groups = Hash.new { |h, k| h[k] = [] }
        n = 0
        rows.each do |r|
          r['qty'].to_i.times do
            groups[[r['mat'].to_s, r['T'].to_f]] << Item.new(r['L'].to_f, r['W'].to_f, r['code'].to_s, r['part'].to_s,
                                                             r['module'].to_s, r['edges'] || {}, n += 1)
          end
        end

        out = groups.sort_by { |(m, t), _| [m, t] }.map do |(mat, t), items|
          b = boards[mat]
          sl = b && b['L'].to_f > 0 ? b['L'].to_f : o['sheet_l'].to_f
          sw = b && b['W'].to_f > 0 ? b['W'].to_f : o['sheet_w'].to_f
          sl, sw = sw, sl if sw > sl
          key = "#{mat}|#{fmt t}"
          rot = rotate[key] == true
          group(mat, t, key, items, sl, sw, kerf, trim, rot, b ? true : false, o['tape_extra'].to_f)
        end
        {
          'groups' => out,
          'settings' => { 'kerf' => kerf, 'trim' => trim, 'sheet_l' => o['sheet_l'].to_f, 'sheet_w' => o['sheet_w'].to_f,
                          'tape_extra' => o['tape_extra'].to_f },
          'sheets' => out.sum { |g| g['sheets'].size },
          'tape_m' => out.sum { |g| g['tape_m'] }.round(1)
        }
      end

      def self.group(mat, t, key, items, sl, sw, kerf, trim, rot, from_library, extra)
        ul = sl - 2 * trim
        uw = sw - 2 * trim
        fits = ->(it) { (it.l <= ul + 1e-6 && it.w <= uw + 1e-6) || (rot && it.w <= ul + 1e-6 && it.l <= uw + 1e-6) }
        good, oversize = items.partition { |it| fits.(it) }
        best = nil
        try = lambda do |list, rng|
          sheets = pack(list, ul, uw, kerf, rot, rng)
          score = [sheets.size, sheets.last ? sheets.last[:y_used] * used_len(sheets.last) : 0]
          best = [score, sheets] if best.nil? || (score <=> best[0]) < 0
        end
        orders(good).each { |list| try.(list, nil) }
        # Then a time-boxed search with varied choices (seeded: same input, same result).
        rng = Random.new(good.size * 7919 + 17)
        t_end = Process.clock_gettime(Process::CLOCK_MONOTONIC) + SEARCH_SECONDS
        tries = 0
        while tries < MAX_TRIES && Process.clock_gettime(Process::CLOCK_MONOTONIC) < t_end
          break if best && best[0][0] <= lower_bound(good, ul, uw)
          try.(good.shuffle(random: rng), rng)
          tries += 1
        end
        sheets = best ? best[1] : []
        area_sheet = sl * sw
        tape = items.sum do |it|
          e = it.edges
          ((e['L1'] ? 1 : 0) + (e['L2'] ? 1 : 0)) * it.l + ((e['W1'] ? 1 : 0) + (e['W2'] ? 1 : 0)) * it.w
        end
        sheet_out = sheets.each_with_index.map do |s, i|
          parts_area = s[:pieces].sum { |p| p[:it].l * p[:it].w }
          {
            'n' => i + 1,
            'pieces' => s[:pieces].map do |p|
              it = p[:it]
              { 'x' => r1(p[:x] + trim), 'y' => r1(p[:y] + trim), 'dx' => p[:dx], 'dy' => p[:dy],
                'L' => it.l, 'W' => it.w, 'code' => it.code, 'part' => it.part, 'module' => it.mod, 'rot' => p[:rot] }
            end,
            'cuts' => s[:cuts].map { |c| c.map { |v| r1(v + trim) } },
            'used' => [r1(used_len(s)), r1(s[:y_used])],
            'parts_m2' => (parts_area / 1e6).round(2),
            'waste_pct' => (100.0 * (1 - parts_area / area_sheet)).round(1)
          }
        end
        parts_area = good.sum { |it| it.l * it.w }
        {
          'key' => key, 'mat' => mat, 'T' => t, 'sheet' => [sl, sw], 'library' => from_library, 'rotate' => rot,
          'parts' => items.size, 'sheets' => sheet_out,
          'parts_m2' => (parts_area / 1e6).round(2),
          'sheets_m2' => (sheet_out.size * area_sheet / 1e6).round(2),
          'waste_pct' => sheet_out.empty? ? 0.0 : (100.0 * (1 - parts_area / (sheet_out.size * area_sheet))).round(1),
          'tape_net_m' => (tape / 1000.0).round(1),
          'tape_m' => (tape / 1000.0 * (1 + extra / 100.0)).round(1),
          'oversize' => oversize.map { |it| { 'code' => it.code, 'part' => it.part, 'L' => it.l, 'W' => it.w } }
        }
      end

      def self.r1(v)
        (v * 10).round / 10.0
      end

      def self.used_len(s)
        s[:pieces].map { |p| p[:x] + p[:dx] }.max || 0
      end

      # Starting part orders (types are taken in this order when scores tie).
      def self.orders(items)
        [
          items.sort_by { |i| [-i.w, -i.l, i.id] },
          items.sort_by { |i| [-i.l, -i.w, i.id] }
        ]
      end

      def self.lower_bound(items, ul, uw)
        (items.sum { |i| i.l * i.w } / (ul * uw)).ceil
      end

      # Identical sizes are one "type" with a stack of items (keeps big jobs fast).
      def self.types_of(list)
        h = {}
        list.each { |it| (h[[it.l, it.w]] ||= []) << it }
        h.map { |(l, w), its| { l: l, w: w, items: its } }
      end

      # Orientations of a type: [dx along the sheet length, dy across, rotated?]
      def self.orients(t, rot)
        o = [[t[:l], t[:w], false]]
        o << [t[:w], t[:l], true] if rot && t[:l] != t[:w]
        o
      end

      # 1. Build strips one at a time, the best-filled one first (a strip that can be
      #    repeated with the parts left is repeated).
      # 2. Put the strips on as few sheets as possible.
      def self.pack(list, ul, uw, kerf, rot, rng = nil)
        types = types_of(list)
        types.shuffle!(random: rng) if rng
        cnt = types.map { |t| t[:items].size }
        strips = []
        while cnt.sum > 0
          widths = []
          types.each_with_index do |t, i|
            next if cnt[i].zero?
            orients(t, rot).each { |_, dy, _| widths << dy if dy <= uw + 1e-6 }
          end
          widths = widths.uniq.sort.reverse
          mw = types.size > BIG_TYPES ? 4 : MAX_WIDTHS
          widths = (widths.first(mw) + widths.last(2)).uniq
          idx = (0...types.size).to_a
          views = [idx, idx.sort_by { |i| [-types[i][:l], -types[i][:w], i] },
                   idx.sort_by { |i| [-(types[i][:l] * types[i][:w]), i] }]
          views = views.first(1) if types.size > BIG_TYPES
          views = views.map do |v|
            pos = v.each_with_index.to_h
            { order: v, by_area: v.sort_by { |i| [-(types[i][:l] * types[i][:w]), pos[i]] } }
          end
          cands = []
          widths.each do |w|
            views.each do |view|
              pat = fill_strip(types, cnt.dup, w, ul, kerf, rot, rng, view)
              next if pat.empty?
              area = pat.sum { |seg| seg.sum { |p| p[1] * p[2] } }
              cands << [[area / (w * ul), w], w, pat]
            end
          end
          break if cands.empty?
          cands = cands.each_with_index.sort_by { |c, k| [-c[0][0], -c[0][1], k] }.map(&:first)
          pick = rng ? cands[rng.rand([cands.size, 3].min)] : cands.first
          w = pick[1]
          pat = pick[2]
          need = Hash.new(0)
          pat.each { |seg| seg.each { |p| need[p[0]] += 1 } }
          repeat = rng.nil? || rng.rand < 0.5
          loop do
            strips << realize(types, cnt, pat, w, ul, kerf)
            break unless repeat && need.all? { |i, n| cnt[i] >= n }
          end
        end
        sheets_of(strips, uw, kerf).map do |group|
          s = { pieces: [], cuts: [], y_used: 0.0 }
          y = 0.0
          group.sort_by { |st| -st[:w] }.each do |st|
            st[:pieces].each { |p| s[:pieces] << p.merge(y: p[:y] + y) }
            st[:cuts].each { |c| s[:cuts] << [c[0], c[1] + y, c[2], c[3] + y] }
            s[:cuts] << [0.0, y + st[:w], ul, y + st[:w]] if y + st[:w] < uw - 1e-6
            y += st[:w] + kerf
          end
          s[:y_used] = y - kerf
          s
        end
      end

      # Take the parts of a strip pattern out of the pool and position them.
      def self.realize(types, cnt, pat, w, ul, kerf)
        st = { pieces: [], cuts: [], w: w }
        x = 0.0
        pat.each do |seg|
          len = seg.first[1]
          y_off = 0.0
          seg.each_with_index do |(i, dx, dy, f), k|
            it = types[i][:items][types[i][:items].size - cnt[i]]
            cnt[i] -= 1
            st[:pieces] << { it: it, x: x, y: y_off, dx: dx, dy: dy, rot: f }
            st[:cuts] << [x, y_off - kerf, x + len, y_off - kerf] if k > 0
            y_off += dy + kerf
          end
          x += len + kerf
          st[:cuts] << [x - kerf, 0.0, x - kerf, w] if x - kerf < ul - 1e-6
        end
        st
      end

      # Strips onto sheets: each sheet takes the set of strips that fills its width best
      # (bounded subset sum in 0.1 mm steps over the distinct strip widths).
      def self.sheets_of(strips, uw, kerf)
        left = strips.sort_by { |st| -st[:w] }
        cap = ((uw + kerf) * 10 + 1e-6).floor
        out = []
        until left.empty?
          by_w = left.group_by { |st| ((st[:w] + kerf) * 10).round }
          ws = by_w.keys.sort.reverse
          reach = Array.new(cap + 1, false)
          reach[0] = true
          parent = Array.new(cap + 1)
          ws.each_with_index do |sz, wi|
            n = by_w[sz].size
            used = Array.new(cap + 1, 0)
            (sz..cap).each do |v|
              next if reach[v] || !reach[v - sz] || used[v - sz] >= n
              reach[v] = true
              used[v] = used[v - sz] + 1
              parent[v] = [v - sz, wi]
            end
          end
          v = cap
          v -= 1 until reach[v]
          take = Hash.new(0)
          while v > 0
            pv, wi = parent[v]
            take[ws[wi]] += 1
            v = pv
          end
          take[ws.first] = 1 if take.empty?
          sheet = []
          take.each { |sz, k| sheet.concat(by_w[sz].first(k)) }
          out << sheet
          left -= sheet
        end
        out
      end

      # Plan one strip along the sheet length: cross-cut segments, each a head part (its
      # length is the segment length) with parts stacked beside it. At every step the
      # segment that fills the strip width best is taken. Returns segments as lists of
      # [type index, dx, dy, rotated?]; cnt is a scratch copy of the counts.
      def self.fill_strip(types, cnt, strip_w, ul, kerf, rot, rng = nil, view = nil)
        view ||= { order: (0...types.size).to_a, by_area: (0...types.size).sort_by { |i| -(types[i][:l] * types[i][:w]) } }
        x = 0.0
        pat = []
        loop do
          room_l = ul - x
          heads = []
          view[:order].each do |i|
            t = types[i]
            next if cnt[i].zero?
            orients(t, rot).each do |dx, dy, f|
              heads << [i, dx, dy, f] if dy <= strip_w + 1e-6 && dx <= room_l + 1e-6
            end
          end
          break if heads.empty?
          heads = heads.each_with_index.sort_by { |h, k| [-(h[1] * h[2]), k] }.map(&:first).first(MAX_HEADS)
          segs = heads.map do |h|
            seg = build_segment(types, cnt, h, strip_w, kerf, rot, view)
            area = seg.sum { |p| p[1] * p[2] }
            [[area / (h[1] * strip_w), area], seg]
          end
          segs = segs.each_with_index.sort_by { |c, k| [-c[0][0], -c[0][1], k] }.map(&:first)
          seg = (rng && segs.size > 1 && rng.rand < 0.3 ? segs[1] : segs[0])[1]
          seg.each { |p| cnt[p[0]] -= 1 }
          pat << seg
          x += seg.first[1] + kerf
        end
        pat
      end

      def self.build_segment(types, cnt, head, strip_w, kerf, rot, view)
        seg = [head]
        used = Hash.new(0)
        used[head[0]] += 1
        room = strip_w - head[2] - kerf
        while room > 0
          pick = nil
          # largest part that fits beside the head (types are pre-sorted by area).
          # Plain while loops, not each + break: same result, but leaving a block with
          # break leaks memory in the browser build of Ruby (ruby.wasm, used by PanelPro Web).
          order = view[:by_area]
          j = 0
          while pick.nil? && j < order.size
            i = order[j]
            j += 1
            next if cnt[i] - used[i] <= 0
            os = orients(types[i], rot)
            k = 0
            while k < os.size
              ex, ey, g = os[k]
              k += 1
              next unless ex <= head[1] + 1e-6 && ey <= room + 1e-6
              pick = [i, ex, ey, g]
              break
            end
          end
          break unless pick
          seg << pick
          used[pick[0]] += 1
          room -= pick[2] + kerf
        end
        seg
      end
    end
  end
end

# encoding: UTF-8
# CSPARTNERS PANEL PRO — module codes for the cut list.
#
#   * Each different module gets a letter: A, B … Z, AA, AB …
#   * Identical modules (same settings and hand paint) share it: A, A1, A2, A3 —
#     numbered in the order they were placed; deleting one renumbers the rest.
#   * Letters are frozen: once a kind of module has a letter it keeps it, and a
#     letter is never reused for something else. A changed copy gets the next
#     new letter (or rejoins its old group if it is changed back).
# Pure Ruby; the model stores the state ({ 'map' => { signature => letter }, 'next' => n }).

require 'digest'
require 'json'

module CSPartners
  module PanelPro
    module Codes
      def self.letter(i)
        s = ''
        i += 1
        while i > 0
          i, r = (i - 1).divmod(26)
          s = (65 + r).chr + s
        end
        s
      end

      def self.canon(o)
        case o
        when Hash then o.keys.map(&:to_s).sort.map { |k| [k, canon(o[k] || o[k.to_sym])] }
        when Array then o.map { |x| canon(x) }
        when Float then o == o.round ? o.round : o.round(3)
        else o
        end
      end

      # Signature of what gets cut: the module's settings plus any hand-painted panels.
      def self.signature(params, painted = {})
        params = params.reject { |k, _| k.to_s == 'hangers' } if params.is_a?(Hash) # look only, nothing cut
        Digest::MD5.hexdigest(JSON.generate([canon(params), canon(painted || {})]))
      end

      # mods: [{ 'id', 'sig', 'order' }] → [codes { id => code }, new state]
      def self.assign(mods, state)
        map = (state && state['map']) ? state['map'].dup : {}
        nxt = (state && state['next']).to_i
        used = map.values
        nxt = [nxt, used.map { |l| index(l) + 1 }.max || 0].max
        codes = {}
        mods.sort_by { |m| m['order'] }.group_by { |m| m['sig'] }.each do |sig, group|
          unless map[sig]
            map[sig] = letter(nxt)
            nxt += 1
          end
          group.sort_by { |m| m['order'] }.each_with_index do |m, i|
            codes[m['id']] = i.zero? ? map[sig] : "#{map[sig]}#{i}"
          end
        end
        [codes, { 'map' => map, 'next' => nxt }]
      end

      # Sort order for codes: A, A1, A2, B … Z, AA.
      def self.sort_key(c)
        c.to_s =~ /\A([A-Z]+)(\d*)\z/ ? [index(Regexp.last_match(1)), Regexp.last_match(2).to_i] : [1e9, 0]
      end

      def self.index(l)
        l.to_s.chars.inject(0) { |a, c| a * 26 + (c.ord - 64) } - 1
      end
    end
  end
end

# encoding: UTF-8
# CSPARTNERS PANEL PRO — module manual (spec sheet per module + project parts page).
# Pure Ruby: counts per module, project totals and the plastic toe-kick bar plan.
# The drawings and the page layout are made in the Configurator (ui/panel.js).

module CSPartners
  module PanelPro
    module Manual
      BAR = 4000.0   # plastic toe kick is sold in 4 m bars
      KERF = 3.0     # saw cut between pieces

      SLIDE = /(?:slide pair, soft-close, (\d+(?:\.\d+)?) mm|runner pair, full extension, NL (\d+(?:\.\d+)?)|drawer set.*NL (\d+(?:\.\d+)?))/.freeze
      HINGE = /\AConcealed hinge/.freeze
      LEG = /\AAdjustable leg/.freeze
      KICK = /\APlastic toe kick, stainless look, (\d+(?:\.\d+)?) mm high: (\d+(?:\.\d+)?) mm\z/.freeze

      # hw: [[item, qty]] of one module → { doors, drawers, hinges, slides => {nl => pairs}, legs }
      def self.counts(hw, movers)
        c = { 'doors' => 0, 'drawers' => 0, 'hinges' => 0, 'slides' => {}, 'legs' => 0 }
        (movers || []).each { |m| c[m['kind'] == 'drawer' ? 'drawers' : 'doors'] += 1 if %w[door drawer].include?(m['kind']) }
        (hw || []).each do |item, q|
          q = q.to_i
          if (m = item.match(SLIDE))
            nl = (m[1] || m[2] || m[3]).to_f
            c['slides'][nl] = (c['slides'][nl] || 0) + q
          elsif item =~ HINGE then c['hinges'] += q
          elsif item =~ LEG then c['legs'] += q
          end
        end
        c
      end

      # Plastic toe-kick pieces: [{ 'h' => height, 'len' => mm, 'code' => module code }]
      def self.kick_pieces(modules)
        modules.flat_map do |m|
          (m['hardware'] || []).flat_map do |item, q|
            k = item.match(KICK)
            k ? Array.new(q.to_i) { { 'h' => k[1].to_f, 'len' => k[2].to_f, 'code' => m['code'] } } : []
          end
        end
      end

      # Cut the pieces from 4 m bars with as little waste as possible: pieces longer than a
      # bar are split (full bars + the rest), then best-fit decreasing — each piece goes in
      # the bar where it leaves the smallest offcut. Per height (100 / 150 are separate bars).
      # Returns [{ 'h', 'bars' => [{ 'cuts' => [{len, code, part}], 'used', 'offcut' }], 'metres', 'pieces' }]
      def self.kick_plan(pieces, bar = BAR, kerf = KERF)
        pieces.group_by { |p| p['h'] }.sort.map do |h, list|
          cuts = []
          list.each do |p|
            len = p['len']
            n = 0
            while len > bar + 1e-6
              n += 1
              cuts << { 'len' => bar, 'code' => p['code'], 'part' => "#{n} (joint)" }
              len -= bar
            end
            cuts << { 'len' => len.round(1), 'code' => p['code'], 'part' => n.positive? ? "#{n + 1} (joint)" : nil }
          end
          bars = []
          cuts.sort_by { |c| -c['len'] }.each do |c|
            need = ->(b) { b['cuts'].empty? ? c['len'] : c['len'] + kerf }
            fit = bars.select { |b| b['used'] + need.call(b) <= bar + 1e-6 }.min_by { |b| bar - b['used'] - need.call(b) }
            unless fit
              fit = { 'cuts' => [], 'used' => 0.0 }
              bars << fit
            end
            fit['used'] += need.call(fit)
            fit['cuts'] << c
          end
          bars.each { |b| b['used'] = b['used'].round(1); b['offcut'] = (bar - b['used']).round(1) }
          { 'h' => h, 'bars' => bars, 'metres' => (list.sum { |p| p['len'] } / 1000.0).round(2), 'pieces' => list.size }
        end
      end

      # One module's page of the manual (both apps build it here).
      # p: normalized params, res: Builder.build(p), lng: 'en' / 'es'.
      def self.module_entry(code, p, res, lng)
        hw = res['hardware']
        {
          'code' => code, 'name' => p['name'].to_s, 'type' => p['type'].to_s,
          'label' => (Params::PRESETS[p['type'].to_s] || {})['label'].to_s,
          'width' => p['width'], 'height' => p['height'], 'depth' => p['depth'], 't' => p['t'],
          'kick' => p['kick_type'].to_s == 'none' ? 0 : p['kick_h'].to_f,
          'mat_carcass' => p['mat_carcass'], 'mat_front' => p['mat_front'],
          'parts' => res['parts'].map { |pt| pt.reject { |k, _| %w[pid note].include?(k) } }, 'movers' => res['movers'],
          'hardware' => hw, 'hardware_l' => hw.map { |it, q| [I18n.text(it, lng), q] },
          'counts' => counts(hw, res['movers']),
          'warnings' => res['warnings'].map { |w| I18n.warn(w, lng) }
        }
      end

      # The whole manual: module pages (entries above, or { 'code', 'name', 'error' }) + project parts.
      def self.project(mods, lng)
        ok = mods.reject { |m| m['error'] }
        {
          'lang' => lng, 'modules' => mods,
          'totals' => totals(ok).map { |it, q| [I18n.text(it, lng), q] },
          'kick' => kick_plan(kick_pieces(ok)), 'bar' => BAR, 'kerf' => KERF
        }
      end

      # Project totals: hardware summed over the modules (items as the builder writes them).
      def self.totals(modules)
        t = Hash.new(0)
        modules.each { |m| (m['hardware'] || []).each { |item, q| t[item] += q.to_i unless item =~ KICK } }
        t.sort_by { |item, _| item }
      end
    end
  end
end

# encoding: UTF-8
# CSPARTNERS PANEL PRO — user presets and finish sets, independent of where they are stored.
# Pure Ruby, shared by the SketchUp plugin (a JSON file in the presets folder) and PanelPro Web
# (kept on the phone). A preset book is a Hash { key => params + 'name' + 'category' }; the file
# format ({ 'panelpro_presets' => 1, 'presets' => book }) is the same in both apps.

module CSPartners
  module PanelPro
    module PresetBook
      module_function

      def key(name)
        name.to_s.downcase.gsub(/[^a-z0-9áéíóúñü]+/, '_').gsub(/\A_|_\z/, '')
      end

      def entry(name, category, params)
        Params.normalize(params).merge('name' => name.to_s, 'category' => category.to_s.empty? ? 'Other' : category.to_s)
      end

      # → [book, key]
      def save(book, name, category, params)
        h = (book || {}).dup
        k = key(name)
        h[k] = entry(name, category, params)
        [h, k]
      end

      # Same name and category, new settings. → book, or nil when the key is unknown.
      def update(book, k, params)
        h = (book || {}).dup
        return nil unless h[k]
        h[k] = entry(h[k]['name'], h[k]['category'] || 'Other', params)
        h
      end

      def delete(book, k)
        h = (book || {}).dup
        h.delete(k)
        h
      end

      def list(book)
        (book || {}).map { |k, v| { 'key' => k, 'label' => v['name'] || k, 'category' => v['category'] || 'Other' } }
                    .sort_by { |p| [p['category'], p['label'].downcase] }
      end

      def export(book)
        { 'panelpro_presets' => 1, 'presets' => book || {} }
      end

      # Adds presets from an exported file (or a bare book); a name that already exists gets
      # " (2)", " (3)"… → [book, number added]
      def import(book, data)
        incoming = data.is_a?(Hash) && data['presets'].is_a?(Hash) ? data['presets'] : data
        raise ArgumentError, 'not a presets file' unless incoming.is_a?(Hash)
        h = (book || {}).dup
        n = 0
        incoming.each_value do |v|
          next unless v.is_a?(Hash)
          name = v['name'].to_s.empty? ? 'Preset' : v['name'].to_s
          base = name
          i = 2
          while h.key?(key(name))
            name = "#{base} (#{i})"
            i += 1
          end
          h[key(name)] = entry(name, v['category'] || 'Other', v)
          n += 1
        end
        [h, n]
      end

      # ------------------------------------------------------------ finish sets
      # Named sets of materials ("Kitchen A: carcass white, fronts Davos Oak").
      def finish_keys
        Params::MAT_KEYS + Params::SAME_MAT.map { |k| "#{k}_same" } + %w[mat_end_same mat_back_front]
      end

      def finish(params)
        finish_keys.each_with_object({}) { |k, o| o[k] = params[k] if params.key?(k) }
      end
    end
  end
end

# encoding: UTF-8
# CSPARTNERS PANEL PRO — material costs from the sheet optimizer result. Pure Ruby.
#
# Material list (kept by the app): one entry per decor —
#   { 'name' => 'Grey Bardolino Oak', 'sheet_l' => 2800, 'sheet_w' => 2070,
#     'thick' => [ { 't' => 18, 'price' => 4500, 'roll_price' => 1200, 'roll_m' => 100 }, … ] }
# Each thickness has its own sheet price and its own edge tape roll (the tape width follows the
# board thickness). Sheets are whole sheets (the optimizer's count) and edge tape is bought in
# whole rolls: needing 1 m more than one roll gives two rolls.

module CSPartners
  module PanelPro
    module Costing
      EPS = 0.01

      def self.num(v)
        v.to_s.tr(',', '.').to_f
      end

      def self.key_of(name)
        name.to_s.strip.downcase.gsub(/\s+/, ' ')
      end

      # The list entry for a material name (case and extra spaces don't matter).
      def self.find(list, name)
        k = key_of(name)
        return nil if k.empty?
        (list || []).find { |e| key_of(e['name']) == k }
      end

      def self.thickness(entry, t)
        return nil unless entry
        (entry['thick'] || []).find { |x| (num(x['t']) - t.to_f).abs < EPS }
      end

      # Sheet sizes for the optimizer, keyed by the material names used in the cut-list rows.
      def self.boards(list, rows)
        out = {}
        (rows || []).each do |r|
          m = r['mat'].to_s
          next if out.key?(m)
          e = find(list, m)
          next unless e && num(e['sheet_l']) > 0 && num(e['sheet_w']) > 0
          out[m] = { 'L' => num(e['sheet_l']), 'W' => num(e['sheet_w']) }
        end
        out
      end

      # Whole rolls needed for a length of tape (metres).
      def self.rolls(tape_m, roll_m)
        return 0 unless tape_m.to_f > 0 && roll_m.to_f > 0
        (tape_m.to_f / roll_m.to_f - 1e-9).ceil
      end

      # opt: Optimizer.run result. defaults: 'roll_price', 'roll_m' for tape with no roll in the list,
      # 'prices' => { "material|T" => price per sheet } (older per-group prices).
      # Adds 'cost' to every group and returns the totals.
      def self.run(opt, list, defaults = {})
        d = defaults || {}
        groups = (opt['groups'] || []).map do |g|
          e = find(list, g['mat'])
          th = thickness(e, g['T'])
          price = th && num(th['price']) > 0 ? num(th['price']) : num((d['prices'] || {})[g['key']])
          own_roll = th && num(th['roll_m']) > 0
          roll_m = own_roll ? num(th['roll_m']) : num(d['roll_m'])
          roll_price = own_roll ? num(th['roll_price']) : num(d['roll_price'])
          n = g['sheets'].size
          tape_m = g['tape_m'].to_f
          r = rolls(tape_m, roll_m)
          c = {
            'listed' => !e.nil?, 'thickness_listed' => !th.nil?,
            'sheets' => n, 'sheet_price' => price, 'sheets_cost' => (n * price).round(2),
            'tape_m' => tape_m, 'roll_m' => roll_m, 'roll_price' => roll_price, 'rolls' => r,
            'tape_left_m' => r > 0 ? (r * roll_m - tape_m).round(1) : 0.0,
            'tape_cost' => (r * roll_price).round(2)
          }
          c['total'] = (c['sheets_cost'] + c['tape_cost']).round(2)
          g['cost'] = c
          c.merge('key' => g['key'], 'mat' => g['mat'], 'T' => g['T'])
        end
        sc = groups.sum { |c| c['sheets_cost'] }.round(2)
        tc = groups.sum { |c| c['tape_cost'] }.round(2)
        opt['cost'] = { 'groups' => groups, 'sheets_cost' => sc, 'tape_cost' => tc,
                        'rolls' => groups.sum { |c| c['rolls'] }, 'total' => (sc + tc).round(2) }
      end
    end
  end
end

# encoding: UTF-8
# CSPARTNERS PANEL PRO — decorative panels for a run of modules (shared by the plugin and PanelPro Web).
#
# A run is a row of modules side by side on one wall (e.g. wall cabinets). For it this plans:
#   bottom — Underpanel: lies flat under the run and hides the joints from below
#   top    — Overpanel: lies flat on top of the run
#   crown  — Crown: a strip on edge on top of the run, up to the ceiling
# Each piece is an ordinary loose Panel module (Params 'panel'), so it is drawn, coded and in the
# cut list like any module. A piece longer than the usable board length is split, preferably on
# the seams between modules (5 modules → 3 + 2), all pieces on the same seams.
#
# Frame: millimetres, x along the run (left → right), y front → back (y = 0 is not special),
# z up from the floor. Each module comes with its offset in that frame; the interface works out
# the offsets (the plugin from the SketchUp model, the web app from the composition).
# Pure Ruby.

module CSPartners
  module PanelPro
    module RunPanels
      KINDS = %w[bottom top crown].freeze
      NAMES = { 'bottom' => 'Underpanel', 'top' => 'Overpanel', 'crown' => 'Crown' }.freeze
      TOL = 2.0 # mm

      def self.r(v)
        (v.to_f * 10).round / 10.0
      end

      def self.fmt(v)
        v = r(v)
        v == v.to_i ? v.to_i.to_s : v.to_s
      end

      # mods: [{ 'code', 'name', 'params', 'off' => [dx, dy, dz], 'res' (optional, a Builder result) }]
      # Returns the run: modules sorted left → right with their extents, and the run's own.
      def self.measure(mods)
        list = []
        warnings = []
        mods.each do |m|
          p = Params.normalize(m['params'] || {})
          res = m['res'] || Builder.build(p)
          off = (m['off'] || [0, 0, 0]).map(&:to_f)
          box = { 'x' => [], 'yb' => [], 'yc' => [], 'yd' => [], 'zl' => [], 'zh' => [] }
          res['parts'].each do |pt|
            next if pt['shape'] == 'cyl' || pt['role'] == 'hardware'
            lo, hi = extents(pt)
            role = pt['role']
            box['zh'] << hi[2]
            box['zl'] << lo[2] unless role == 'base'
            if %w[carcass skin frame back top].include?(role)
              box['x'] << lo[0] << hi[0]
              box['yb'] << hi[1]
            end
            box['yc'] << lo[1] if %w[carcass frame].include?(role)
            box['yd'] << lo[1] if role == 'front'
          end
          next if box['x'].empty?
          cf = box['yc'].empty? ? 0.0 : box['yc'].min
          list << {
            'code' => m['code'].to_s, 'name' => (m['name'] || p['name']).to_s,
            'x0' => r(box['x'].min + off[0]), 'x1' => r(box['x'].max + off[0]),
            'front' => r(cf + off[1]), 'door' => r((box['yd'].empty? ? cf : [box['yd'].min, cf].min) + off[1]),
            'back' => r(box['yb'].max + off[1]),
            'z_lo' => r((box['zl'].empty? ? 0.0 : box['zl'].min) + off[2]), 'z_hi' => r(box['zh'].max + off[2]),
            't' => p['t'].to_f, 'mat_front' => p['mat_front'].to_s, 'mat_skin' => p['mat_skin'].to_s
          }
        end
        raise BuildError, 'Select one or more modules first.' if list.empty?
        list.sort_by! { |x| x['x0'] }
        i = 1
        while i < list.size
          a = list[i - 1]
          b = list[i]
          gap = b['x0'] - a['x1']
          warnings << "Gap of #{fmt gap} mm between #{a['code']} and #{b['code']} — the panel spans it." if gap > TOL
          warnings << "#{a['code']} and #{b['code']} overlap by #{fmt(-gap)} mm." if gap < -TOL
          i += 1
        end
        lows = list.map { |x| x['z_lo'] }
        highs = list.map { |x| x['z_hi'] }
        warnings << 'The modules are not level underneath — the underpanel goes under the lowest one.' if lows.max - lows.min > TOL
        warnings << 'The modules are not level on top — the overpanel and crown sit on the highest one.' if highs.max - highs.min > TOL
        fronts = list.map { |x| x['front'] }
        warnings << 'The fronts of the modules are not in line — the panels follow the one furthest forward.' if fronts.max - fronts.min > TOL
        {
          'mods' => list, 'x0' => list.first['x0'], 'x1' => list.last['x1'],
          'front' => fronts.min, 'door' => list.map { |x| x['door'] }.min, 'back' => list.map { |x| x['back'] }.max,
          'z_lo' => lows.min, 'z_hi' => highs.max, 't' => list.first['t'],
          'mat_front' => list.first['mat_front'], 'mat_skin' => list.first['mat_skin'],
          'seams' => (1...list.size).map { |k| { 'i' => k, 'x' => r((list[k - 1]['x1'] + list[k]['x0']) / 2.0), 'between' => "#{list[k - 1]['code']} | #{list[k]['code']}" } },
          'warnings' => warnings
        }
      end

      # [[x, y, z] min, [x, y, z] max] of a prism part (module mm).
      def self.extents(pt)
        u, v = { 'x' => %w[y z], 'y' => %w[x z], 'z' => %w[x y] }[pt['axis']]
        idx = { 'x' => 0, 'y' => 1, 'z' => 2 }
        lo = [0.0, 0.0, 0.0]
        hi = [0.0, 0.0, 0.0]
        a = idx[pt['axis']]
        lo[a] = pt['pos'].to_f
        hi[a] = pt['pos'].to_f + pt['thk'].to_f
        us = pt['pts'].map { |q| q[0].to_f }
        vs = pt['pts'].map { |q| q[1].to_f }
        lo[idx[u]] = us.min
        hi[idx[u]] = us.max
        lo[idx[v]] = vs.min
        hi[idx[v]] = vs.max
        [lo, hi]
      end

      DEFAULT_OPTS = {
        'front' => 'doors', 'front_oh' => 0.0, 'side_l' => 0.0, 'side_r' => 0.0, 'eb' => 'front',
        'h_mode' => 'ceiling', 'ceiling' => 2400.0, 'height' => 100.0
      }.freeze

      # run: from measure. opts:
      #   'pieces' => { 'bottom' => { …kind options }, 'crown' => { … } }  (only the kinds wanted)
      #       kind options: 'front' ('doors' | 'carcass' | 'custom'), 'front_oh' (custom: mm in front of
      #       the carcass), 'side_l', 'side_r' (overhang mm), 'eb' (panel_eb), 'mat', 't',
      #       crown: 'h_mode' ('ceiling' | 'height'), 'ceiling' (mm from the floor), 'height' (mm)
      #   'split' => 'auto' | 'middle' | [seam numbers], 'sheet_l', 'trim', 'lang'
      # Returns { 'pieces' => [{ 'kind', 'name', 'params', 'origin' => [x, y, z], 'size' => [L, W, T] }],
      #           'split', 'cuts' (x of each joint), 'usable', 'warnings', 'errors' }
      def self.plan(run, opts)
        lng = opts['lang'] || 'en'
        usable = (opts['sheet_l'] || Optimizer::DEFAULTS['sheet_l']).to_f - 2 * (opts['trim'] || Optimizer::DEFAULTS['trim']).to_f
        want = opts['pieces'].is_a?(Hash) ? opts['pieces'] : {}
        kinds = KINDS.select { |k| want[k] }
        errors = []
        warnings = (run['warnings'] || []).dup
        errors << 'Choose at least one piece: under, above or crown.' if kinds.empty?
        o = {}
        kinds.each { |k| o[k] = DEFAULT_OPTS.merge(want[k].is_a?(Hash) ? want[k] : {}) }
        # length of each kind (the run plus its side overhangs)
        oh = ->(k) { [o[k]['side_l'].to_f, o[k]['side_r'].to_f] }
        max_l = kinds.map { |k| oh.(k)[0] }.max || 0.0
        max_r = kinds.map { |k| oh.(k)[1] }.max || 0.0
        cuts, split = cut_points(run, opts['split'], usable, max_l, max_r)
        pieces = []
        kinds.each do |k| # rubocop:disable Metrics/BlockLength
          ko = o[k]
          t = (ko['t'] || run['t']).to_f
          t = run['t'].to_f if t <= 0
          mat = ko['mat'].to_s.empty? ? run['mat_front'] : ko['mat'].to_s
          fy = case ko['front']
               when 'carcass' then run['front']
               when 'custom' then run['front'] - ko['front_oh'].to_f
               else run['door']
               end
          l0 = run['x0'] - ko['side_l'].to_f
          l1 = run['x1'] + ko['side_r'].to_f
          xs = [l0] + cuts + [l1]
          depth = run['back'] - fy
          z0, h = case k
                  when 'bottom' then [run['z_lo'] - t, t]
                  when 'top' then [run['z_hi'], t]
                  else
                    base = run['z_hi'] + (o['top'] ? (o['top']['t'] || run['t']).to_f : 0.0)
                    hh = ko['h_mode'] == 'height' ? ko['height'].to_f : ko['ceiling'].to_f - base
                    errors << "Crown: the ceiling (#{fmt ko['ceiling']} mm) must be above the top of the run (#{fmt base} mm)." if hh <= 0.5
                    [base, hh]
                  end
          next if h <= 0.5
          n = xs.size - 1
          j = 0
          while j < n
            len = xs[j + 1] - xs[j]
            name = NAMES[k] + (n > 1 ? " #{j + 1}/#{n}" : '')
            q = {
              'name' => I18n.t(name.sub(/ \d+\/\d+\z/, ''), lng) + (n > 1 ? " #{j + 1}/#{n}" : ''),
              'panel' => true, 'panel_kind' => k, 'width' => r(len), 'kick_type' => 'none',
              't' => t, 'panel_t_same' => true, 'panel_eb' => ko['eb'].to_s.empty? ? 'front' : ko['eb'],
              'mat_top' => mat, 'mat_top_same' => false, 'mat_skin' => mat, 'mat_skin_same' => false,
              'elevation' => r([z0, 0].max)
            }
            if k == 'crown'
              q['height'] = r(h)
              q['depth'] = t
            else
              q['height'] = t
              q['depth'] = r(depth)
            end
            size = k == 'crown' ? [r(len), r(h), t] : [r(len), r(depth), t]
            warnings << "#{fmt size[0]} mm piece (#{q['name']}) is longer than the board (#{fmt usable} mm usable)." if size[0] > usable + 0.05
            pieces << { 'kind' => k, 'name' => q['name'], 'params' => Params.normalize(q),
                        'origin' => [r(xs[j]), r(fy), r(z0)], 'size' => size }
            j += 1
          end
        end
        { 'pieces' => pieces, 'split' => split, 'cuts' => cuts.map { |c| r(c) }, 'usable' => r(usable),
          'seams' => run['seams'], 'warnings' => warnings.uniq.map { |w| I18n.warn(w, lng) }, 'errors' => errors.uniq.map { |w| I18n.warn(w, lng) } }
      end

      # Where the long pieces are cut (x of each joint) and which split was used.
      # auto: fewest pieces, cut only on module seams, as even as possible; if a single module is
      # longer than the board, equal pieces ('middle'). A list of seam numbers is used as given.
      def self.cut_points(run, split, usable, oh_l, oh_r)
        mods = run['mods']
        total = run['x1'] - run['x0'] + oh_l + oh_r
        seams = run['seams'] || []
        if split.is_a?(Array)
          xs = split.map(&:to_i).uniq.sort.map { |i| seams.find { |s| s['i'] == i } }.compact.map { |s| s['x'] }
          return [xs, split.map(&:to_i).uniq.sort]
        end
        return [[], []] if total <= usable + 0.05
        if split.to_s != 'middle'
          best = seam_split(mods, seams, usable, oh_l, oh_r)
          return [best.map { |i| seams.find { |s| s['i'] == i }['x'] }, best] if best
        end
        n = (total / usable).ceil
        step = total / n
        [(1...n).map { |k| run['x0'] - oh_l + step * k }, 'middle']
      end

      # Fewest pieces with every piece ≤ usable, cutting only on seams; among those the most even
      # (smallest longest piece), and on a tie the longer pieces first (5 modules → 3 + 2).
      # nil when no seam split works.
      def self.seam_split(mods, seams, usable, oh_l, oh_r)
        return nil if seams.empty?
        edges = [mods.first['x0'] - oh_l] + seams.map { |s| s['x'] } + [mods.last['x1'] + oh_r]
        ids = seams.map { |s| s['i'] }
        k = 1
        found = nil
        while k <= ids.size && found.nil?
          best = nil
          ids.combination(k).each do |cut|
            pts = [edges.first] + cut.map { |c| edges[c] } + [edges.last]
            lens = pts.each_cons(2).map { |a, b| b - a }
            next if lens.max > usable + 0.05
            key = [lens.max.round(1)] + lens.map { |l| -l.round(1) }
            best = [key, cut] if best.nil? || (key <=> best[0]) < 0
          end
          found = best && best[1]
          k += 1
        end
        found
      end
    end
  end
end

# encoding: UTF-8
# CSPARTNERS PANEL PRO — the room: modules placed anywhere (from the SketchUp model), sorted into
# walls by the way they face, plus a plan of the whole space. Shared by the plugin (export) and
# PanelPro Web (composition, room view, manual). Pure Ruby.
#
# Each module's place: 'room' => { 'x', 'y', 'z' (mm, the module's origin = its left-front-bottom
# corner), 'rot' (degrees: the module's width direction turned from +x, counter-clockwise seen
# from above) }. A module's front faces −y in its own axes, its back is +y (against the wall).

module CSPartners
  module PanelPro
    module Room
      ANGLE_TOL = 3.0   # degrees: modules within this face the same way
      LINE_TOL = 250.0  # mm: backs within this are on the same wall line

      def self.r(v)
        (v.to_f * 10).round / 10.0
      end

      def self.norm_deg(a)
        a = a.to_f % 360.0
        a += 360.0 if a.negative?
        a
      end

      # mods: [{ 'id', 'code', 'params', 'room' => {...}, 'bbox' (optional: [[min], [max]] module mm) }]
      # Returns { 'walls' => [{ 'id', 'name', 'rot', 'origin' => [x, y], 'u' => [ux, uy], 'n' => [nx, ny],
      #   'length', 'mods' => [{ 'id', 'code', 'along', 'perp', 'z', 'x0', 'x1' }] }],
      #   'plan' => [{ 'id', 'code', 'wall', 'pts' => [[x, y]×4], 'front' => [[x, y]×2] }], 'box' => [x0, y0, x1, y1] }
      def self.layout(mods, lng = 'en')
        items = []
        mods.each do |m|
          rm = m['room']
          next unless rm.is_a?(Hash)
          bb = m['bbox'] || Builder.build(Params.normalize(m['params'] || {}))['bbox']
          a = norm_deg(rm['rot']) * Math::PI / 180.0
          u = [Math.cos(a), Math.sin(a)]
          n = [-Math.sin(a), Math.cos(a)]
          o = [rm['x'].to_f, rm['y'].to_f]
          back = o[0] * n[0] + o[1] * n[1] + bb[1][1].to_f # where its back is, across the wall
          items << { 'm' => m, 'deg' => norm_deg(rm['rot']), 'u' => u, 'n' => n, 'o' => o, 'z' => rm['z'].to_f, 'bb' => bb, 'back' => back }
        end
        walls = []
        items.sort_by { |it| [it['deg'], it['back']] }.each do |it|
          w = walls.find do |x|
            d = (x['deg'] - it['deg']).abs
            d = 360.0 - d if d > 180.0
            d <= ANGLE_TOL && (x['back'] - it['back']).abs <= LINE_TOL
          end
          if w
            w['items'] << it
          else
            walls << { 'deg' => it['deg'], 'back' => it['back'], 'u' => it['u'], 'n' => it['n'], 'items' => [it] }
          end
        end
        plan = []
        out = walls.each_with_index.map do |w, i|
          u = w['u']
          n = w['n']
          lefts = w['items'].map { |it| it['o'][0] * u[0] + it['o'][1] * u[1] + it['bb'][0][0].to_f }
          start = lefts.min
          ms = w['items'].map do |it|
            along = it['o'][0] * u[0] + it['o'][1] * u[1] - start
            perp = it['o'][0] * n[0] + it['o'][1] * n[1]
            { 'id' => it['m']['id'], 'code' => it['m']['code'], 'along' => r(along), 'perp' => r(perp), 'z' => r(it['z']),
              'x0' => r(along + it['bb'][0][0].to_f), 'x1' => r(along + it['bb'][1][0].to_f) }
          end.sort_by { |x| [x['x0'], x['z']] }
          w['items'].each do |it|
            b = it['bb']
            corner = ->(x, y) { [r(it['o'][0] + u[0] * x + n[0] * y), r(it['o'][1] + u[1] * x + n[1] * y)] }
            plan << { 'id' => it['m']['id'], 'code' => it['m']['code'], 'wall' => i, 'z' => r(it['z']),
                      'h' => r(b[1][2].to_f - b[0][2].to_f),
                      'pts' => [corner.(b[0][0], b[0][1]), corner.(b[1][0], b[0][1]), corner.(b[1][0], b[1][1]), corner.(b[0][0], b[1][1])],
                      'front' => [corner.(b[0][0], b[0][1]), corner.(b[1][0], b[0][1])] }
          end
          { 'id' => i, 'name' => "#{I18n.t('Wall', lng)} #{i + 1}", 'rot' => r(w['deg']),
            'origin' => [r(u[0] * start), r(u[1] * start)], 'u' => u.map { |v| v.round(6) }, 'n' => n.map { |v| v.round(6) },
            'length' => r(ms.map { |x| x['x1'] }.max.to_f - ms.map { |x| x['x0'] }.min.to_f), 'mods' => ms }
        end
        xs = plan.flat_map { |p| p['pts'].map(&:first) }
        ys = plan.flat_map { |p| p['pts'].map(&:last) }
        { 'walls' => out, 'plan' => plan, 'box' => xs.empty? ? nil : [xs.min, ys.min, xs.max, ys.max] }
      end
    end
  end
end

module CSPartners; module PanelPro; VERSION = '0.3.35' unless defined?(VERSION); end; end
# encoding: UTF-8
# CSPARTNERS PANEL PRO Web — bridge between the web app (JavaScript) and the shared module
# engine (src/csp_panel_pro/core/*.rb, loaded unchanged, the same files the SketchUp plugin uses).
# Web-only glue: JSON in, JSON out, calling core functions. No module rules live here — those
# belong in core/ so the plugin gets them too.

require 'json'

module CSPartners
  module PanelPro
    module Web
      module_function

      # Called from JavaScript: method name + JSON argument → JSON { ok, data | error }.
      def call(method, json)
        arg = json.to_s.empty? ? {} : JSON.parse(json)
        m = "api_#{method}"
        raise ArgumentError, "unknown call #{method}" unless respond_to?(m)
        JSON.generate('ok' => true, 'data' => send(m, arg))
      rescue BuildError => e
        JSON.generate('ok' => false, 'error' => I18n.warn(e.message, @lang), 'build' => true)
      rescue StandardError, ScriptError => e
        JSON.generate('ok' => false, 'error' => "#{e.class}: #{e.message}", 'where' => (e.backtrace || []).first(3))
      end

      def lang_of(a)
        @lang = a['lang'] == 'es' ? 'es' : 'en'
      end

      # Everything the app needs to draw its menus.
      def api_info(_a)
        {
          'version' => (defined?(VERSION) ? VERSION : '?'),
          'presets' => Params.preset_list.map do |p|
            cat, name = p['label'].split(' — ', 2)
            { 'key' => p['key'], 'label' => p['label'], 'category' => name ? cat : 'Other', 'name' => name || cat }
          end,
          'choices' => Params::CHOICES, 'fronts' => Params::FRONTS, 'hinges' => Params::HINGES,
          'kick_plastic_h' => Params::KICK_PLASTIC_H, 'defaults' => Params::DEFAULTS,
          'opt_defaults' => Optimizer::DEFAULTS,
          # part names for Settings › Part names (custom names go into the cut list)
          'parts' => Names::PARTS.map { |en, es| { 'en' => en, 'en_label' => Names::DEFAULTS['en'][en], 'es' => es } }
        }
      end

      def api_preset(a)
        Params.preset(a['key'].to_s)
      end

      # The room: modules placed anywhere (from SketchUp), sorted into walls, and the plan.
      def api_room(a)
        Room.layout(a['mods'] || [], lang_of(a))
      end

      # Panels for a run (composition): measure the picked modules, then plan the pieces.
      def api_run_measure(a)
        RunPanels.measure(a['mods'] || [])
      end

      def api_run_plan(a)
        RunPanels.plan(a['run'] || {}, (a['opts'] || {}).merge('lang' => lang_of(a)))
      end

      # Cut list: edge banding on / off for one side ('L1' …) or 'all' of some panels.
      def api_edge_set(a)
        Cutlist.set_edges(a['params'] || {}, a['pids'] || [], a['side'].to_s, a['on'] ? true : false)
      end

      def api_normalize(a)
        Params.normalize(a['params'] || {})
      end

      # Fridge enclosure: size the module around the fridge (same as the plugin).
      def api_fridge_fit(a)
        Params.normalize(Params.fridge_fit(Params.normalize(a['params'] || {})))
      end

      # Left ↔ right (the plugin's flip when placing).
      def api_mirror(a)
        Params.normalize(Params.mirrored(Params.normalize(a['params'] || {})))
      end

      # One module → panels, doors / drawers, hardware, warnings (what the 3D view needs).
      def api_build(a)
        lng = lang_of(a)
        p = Params.normalize(a['params'] || {})
        res = Builder.build(p)
        {
          'params' => p,
          'parts' => res['parts'], 'movers' => res['movers'], 'bbox' => res['bbox'], 'layout' => res['layout'], 'nooks' => res['nooks'],
          'boxes' => res['boxes'],
          'hardware' => res['hardware'], 'hardware_l' => res['hardware'].map { |it, q| [I18n.text(it, lng), q] },
          'warnings' => res['warnings'].map { |w| I18n.warn(w, lng) }
        }
      end

      # Module codes (A, A1, B…) for a project: modules [{ 'id', 'order', 'params' }] + saved state.
      def codes_for(mods, state)
        info = mods.map do |m|
          { 'id' => m['id'].to_s, 'order' => m['order'].to_i, 'sig' => Codes.signature(Params.normalize(m['params'] || {}), {}) }
        end
        Codes.assign(info, state)
      end

      def api_codes(a)
        codes, state = codes_for(a['modules'] || [], a['codes_state'])
        { 'codes' => codes, 'codes_state' => state }
      end

      # Every module of a site, built and sorted by code.
      def built_modules(a, lng)
        mods = a['modules'] || []
        codes, state = codes_for(mods, a['codes_state'])
        built = mods.map do |m|
          p = Params.normalize(m['params'] || {})
          code = codes[m['id'].to_s]
          begin
            { 'code' => code, 'id' => m['id'].to_s, 'name' => p['name'].to_s, 'p' => p, 'res' => Builder.build(p) }
          rescue BuildError => e
            { 'code' => code, 'name' => p['name'].to_s, 'p' => p, 'error' => I18n.warn(e.message, lng),
              'res' => { 'parts' => [], 'hardware' => [], 'warnings' => ["not built: #{e.message}"], 'movers' => [] } }
          end
        end
        [built.sort_by { |b| Codes.sort_key(b['code']) }, codes, state]
      end

      # Site outputs: cut list (+ CSV), module manual, toe-kick bar plan.
      # a: { 'modules' => [{ 'id', 'order', 'params' }], 'codes_state', 'lang',
      #      'names' => { lang => { part => custom name } }, 'opt' => { sheet_l, sheet_w, … } }
      def api_project(a)
        lng = lang_of(a)
        built, codes, state = built_modules(a, lng)
        opt = a['opt'] || {}
        cut = Cutlist.compile(built.map { |b| { 'code' => b['code'], 'id' => b['id'], 'name' => b['name'], 'res' => b['res'] } }, {},
                              'lang' => lng, 'names' => ((a['names'] || {})[lng] || {}),
                              'sheet_l' => opt['sheet_l'], 'sheet_w' => opt['sheet_w'])
        cut['csv'] = Cutlist.to_csv(cut)
        cut['groups'] = { 'mat' => Cutlist.grouped(cut, false), 'mat_t' => Cutlist.grouped(cut, true) }
        manual = Manual.project(built.map do |b|
          b['error'] ? { 'code' => b['code'], 'name' => b['name'], 'error' => b['error'] } : Manual.module_entry(b['code'], b['p'], b['res'], lng)
        end, lng)
        manual['modules'].each { |m| m.delete('parts'); m.delete('movers') } unless a['with_parts']
        {
          'codes' => codes, 'codes_state' => state, 'cutlist' => cut,
          'manual' => manual['modules'].reject { |m| m['error'] }, 'manual_doc' => manual,
          'totals' => manual['totals'], 'kick' => manual['kick'], 'bar' => manual['bar'], 'kerf' => manual['kerf'],
          'errors' => built.select { |b| b['error'] }.map { |b| { 'code' => b['code'], 'error' => b['error'] } }
        }
      end

      # Sheet optimizer over cut-list rows (supplier settings in opt: kerf, trim, sheet_l, sheet_w,
      # tape_extra, rotate { "material|T" => true }).
      # With the app's material list (a['materials']): its sheet sizes, and the cost of every
      # group in whole sheets and whole edge tape rolls (Costing).
      def api_optimize(a)
        rows = a['rows'] || []
        list = a['materials'] || []
        res = Optimizer.run(rows, Costing.boards(list, rows), a['opt'] || {})
        Costing.run(res, list, a['costs'] || {})
        res
      end

      # ---------------------------------------------------------------- presets (book kept by the app)
      def api_presets_list(a)
        PresetBook.list(a['book'])
      end

      def api_presets_save(a)
        book, key = PresetBook.save(a['book'], a['name'], a['category'], a['params'] || {})
        { 'book' => book, 'key' => key }
      end

      def api_presets_update(a)
        { 'book' => PresetBook.update(a['book'], a['key'].to_s, a['params'] || {}) || a['book'] }
      end

      def api_presets_delete(a)
        { 'book' => PresetBook.delete(a['book'], a['key'].to_s) }
      end

      def api_presets_import(a)
        book, n = PresetBook.import(a['book'], a['data'])
        { 'book' => book, 'added' => n }
      end

      def api_presets_export(a)
        PresetBook.export(a['book'])
      end

      def api_preset_params(a)
        Params.normalize((a['book'] || {})[a['key'].to_s] || {})
      end

      def api_finish(a)
        PresetBook.finish(a['params'] || {})
      end
    end
  end
end
